About BMs, foods, meds, etc.  I have and will continue to highly recommend this app. to people with any chronic health issues.

When I first downloaded, I wasn't sure what to expect.  After using it, I was very impressed with the app and their support.  Many apps just want your money but don't worry about the individual, not this one.... they are EXCEPTIONAL!!!  Best money I spent on an app yet.
...diet and this is really helping me see what triggers me. What a great app! Excellent options throughout and very stable.

This app helped me discover what was causing my G.I. issues. And now I'm using it to help me with my allergies.  The database is somewhat sparse in terms of ingredients in things but I've been adding them myself in hopes that someone else can use them. Also the instructions are pretty straightforward but the explanation on scores and ratios in your analysis is a little difficult to understand.  It would be helpful if there was a more detailed explanation on score and ratio and how you could use each.

Overall this app is definitely worth three dollars.

reviews.t: Finally an app to track symptoms and food
reviews.b: I believe food is medicine. However, it is a journey to figure out what is the best foods for my body and how my body responds to each meal. I love this apps ability to track my moods, symptoms, and food. Thanks!
Perfect for being able to track food, symptom and severity - and have this specific/detailed information accessible for meetings with my doctor.
After I figured it out, keeping track of what you put into your body and what comes out it will get easier to log. Still putting in input for meals, but I'll get it. And so will you.

I want to track my food to see what causes my hives. But I didn't realize you could only track the symptoms they have on their list.  Also I might be allergic to a minor ingredient but I can't list anything that is not listed in their tracker. It's probably easier for me to just use a blank journal, too bad.
This app is amazing and incredibly easy to use! The only thing I would consider changing is having more foods available to search.

This app helped me figure out what was causing my GI issues. I logged a couple weeks of food and voila, gluten and dairy are my culprits! 

One helpful hint to anyone buying the app: when logging food, make sure all the ingredients are listed. If gluten is the problem but every time you eat something with gluten you just say "pizza" instead of saying "pizza" and then listing all the ingredients such as flour, oil, etc. you won't be able to figure out what the problem is. Logging ingredients makes everything easier.

A note to the app developers: you guys are awesome. Seriously, this app is amazing. I just have a couple of suggestions. Maybe a more clean/modern user interface? But that's not necessary; the app works great as is.

reviews.t: This was just what I needed to track my routine!
reviews.b: This was just what o needed to track my routine. Excellent app!

My dr asked me to keep a dIly log of over ten symptoms while we play with medications, supplements, and diet. So, I googled "app to track symptoms." The first one I tried was free and did not work. My symptoms is 2.99 and perfect! This app does everything I want and more. It is easy to use, clean design, and extremely helpful. Thanks for making it!

I have so many health problems and trying to figure out what is causing what is difficult for the specialists and I. I have found it easy so far and hope that I can figure out how to chart what each specialist needs. It allows for diversity of conditions by allowing you to add your own symptoms. I have lots of ideas for growth of this app and so far live it. This is the first review I have ever written. Keep up the good work!
Looks promising, but cannot enter the quantity of a food item.

reviews.t: Just what I needed! Love it!
reviews.b: I was looking for an easy way to track my food and symptoms. This app is perfect! So easy to use. Like other reviewers, I don't understand the people that had challenges. I think they didn't understand the basic, simple functionality. I've only used it for a few days now, so I haven't gotten to try the analysis portion but I'm interested to see if that works. For me that's just a bonus. I'm thinking I have to figure out this food/symptom mystery on my own. Speaking of bonuses, the app stores what you've eaten recently for breakfast, lunch, etc. so if you eat the same thing, it's extra easy to enter.

This app is super easy to use, and is perfect for tracking foods/symptoms. ( I am on an elimination diet and need to track those things.) Within 15 minutes of purchasing, I had put in all items I had eaten for the day, along with adding the supplements I was taking. I'm not sure what the negative reviews are about--I read the directions when I first loaded up and was easily able to figure out how to get all my items put in.

reviews.t: Just what I need for a reasonable price
reviews.b:
I don't get the recent negative reviews. This app is actually easy to use. Perhaps I'm tech savvy and I'm really invested in my health right now...? 🤷🏻‍♀️ I actually love how powerful and flexible it is for all the types of entries I can log. This app doesn't require "a lot of work" as a reviewer implied. It's actually pretty simple, once you learn how to use it for your own needs. 

You can even search supplement or food items by scanning their barcode. If it's not already entered in the database, you can enter your own and make it private if you don't want to share the data. You're not required to enter all of the item's details, just the name. I actually really appreciate the data entry's flexibility. Most of the time, I rather use my simple private entries without too much info on all of its ingredients. Sometimes I do want to enter all of the ingredients of a meal, without needing to know the ingredients' details of their nutrition content/makeup because I know I've purchased great quality foods or supplements already, after researching their makeup. 

This is an app that allows for any type of user. If you want more details, it's perfect. If you want less details, it works just as well.

And if someone finds that it's too much work, perhaps they're not that invested in their health because they're not suffering from major ailments or going through major life changes that do require a lot of meticulous monitoring and observation of symptoms (good or bad) vs. nutrition vs. sleep, among other habits / activities.

This is the type of app ANYONE dealing with any type of illness should be pointed to so they can track what they're consuming, how they're sleeping, what they're doing, and what they're feeling, so they can later study the patterns that help better identify cause and effect. Things MUST be logged because our daily routines are complex or change, and we forget what we ate and how we felt throughout the day.

There was another app that offered me similar features but it cost double the price (downloaded 7/2017). That app's free version had major limitations like tracking up to 5 symptoms. So I figured I'd give this app a try for half the price, and it was money well spent. 💰👍🏼👍🏼

I'm very pleased with this app. Good purchase for users who want or need to log all of their common symptoms, their nourishment and sleep patterns, among other daily habits, in order to identify patterns of cause and effect. I highly recommend this to anyone suffering brain chemical disorders including depression, anxiety, and ADD. As well as people with any type of allergy, including asthma and any other auto immune disorder. 💜☯️
This app has potential, but it's just too hard to use. It's difficult to navigate and way too tedious for what it is. The developer should hire a good UI/UX designer.

Decent app for recording eating habits and symptoms. It helped me discover my allergy issue. The pre-populated food list is small, but it is easy to add more that are specific to your diet. The analysis tool is somewhat helpful, I'm not sure I quite understand exactly how to use it, but it does provide some information and symptoms related to food over time.
Too time consuming to use.  The database of foods is very limited.  Very hard to use the app. They have my $3 bucks and I have a lot of nothing.  Don't buy this!
Does not work correctly. Cannot enter food diary properly

I'm a fan. The most used app on my phone at the moment, somewhat surprisingly. Although a bit limited (e.g. I'm exporting to Excel to get the analysis I need). Please keep up the development guys! 

Pros: simple, easy to enter most things, analysis seems to work reasonably well, very flexible entry / categories

To improve: UI, add visualizations (e.g. Symptom frequency), clean up online food database, streamline UX, CSV output data quality, add ability to incorporate symptom severity and food quantities into analysis

Beginning to be my Go to App. Always room for improvement.  Wish could copy & paste symptoms when they are still same. 

Update: 6/10 still <3 it.  Wish List: it could incorporate location (optionally) & show basic weather for that location to see how it affects symptoms.  Also would be great to be able to have backup to a cloud app. And have option to export .csv file to upload to Microsoft Health Vault or Health Tap for my docs.  This is a Valuable App I expect to get better.  

It has Almost replaced my pain diary & GI Monitor among others. Getting There :)
Not necessarily great for average meal tracking for dieting, but super for tracking symptoms as well as "bodily functions." I couldn't find anything else comparable.
I enjoy this app, it's easy to use, and I'm thankful for the data it compiles and analyzes
Love the app.  Hate that it crashes almost every time I am inputting my food items with my iPad.  This only started with the last update.  Prior to that it had never crashed.  Now, almost every time.
Let's me keep track of not only food but also energy levels, symptoms, bowel movements, medications and supplements among other things in one app. Terrific!

I have loved this app so far. I have been using it for several months now. I am able to easily print data reports of my food/symptom log to share with my doctor. I have been able to recognize food sensitivities that I have. Now that I have been able to identify the source of stomach pain, I have been able to avoid foods that cause stomach pains. 

Thank you to the creators of this app! You have helped me in my new dietary journey!

I've off and on tracked food with my Up3 app; I stop because it gets awkward and time consuming. My doctor asked me to track symptoms and food for 8 weeks, so I needed something else, and found the mySymptoms app. I like the variety of categories for tracking, helps to quickly document events as you go. It is nice that the app is flexible enough to let you track to different levels of detail. Favorites list, including 'my recipe' additions, keeps regularly occurring items at your fingertips.

reviews.t: Didn't save anything, crashes when entering info
reviews.b: This app isn't very intuitive. When I finally got everything entered properly (after a few crashes) I went back the next day and all the information was gone. Want a refund.
I've used this app for years now and I am very happy with it. It's extremely helpful to keep track of everything. Highly recommend!

Highly recommend this app.  The premise is simple you input your food intake and report your symptoms, the result is a range of easy to read graphs related to how different foods affect you. I need to be able to track my symptoms overtime and eliminate allergens.  This app is essential for those with celiac's or chronic diseases which benefit from identifying and tracking your diet.  I've made a few requests, but it would be nice to see physicians adopt this more broadly.  Worth the money.  The other free apps, have useful feature that are in-app purchases (a gimmick to get people to download it).

I love this app so much. For the past 3 years, I've struggled with eating and the symptoms it's caused. My mum suggested I track everything I eat and how it makes me feel for when we go to the doctor. This app includes everything I could ask for and more. Could not say better things about it. The only thing I ask is PLEASE ADD NOTIFICATIONS TO REMIND ME!! It would be SO helpful to be able to set reminders to both eat and track my food. I often forget until later when my reminders app tells me to and end up having to rack my brain to remember what I ate that day. It would be amazing if I could set timed notifications for when I normally eat lunch and dinner (12:45 and 7:30).

Very comprehensive, and user friendly! Lots of great options, but some things could be better. Each entry has a start time, but not an end time. A headache, for example, is helpful to track start and end times.

Truly impressive app, makes keeping track of the effects of your food intake manageable and not a huge burden. 

Where it is lacking is the food search/catalog. 20 oz bottle of Coke?? Can get Diet Coke in iterations I did not know existed. But this is enough for the most part, just it is it's only glaring weakness. 

If Wt and portion sizing was incorporated I am sure workout fanatics would like it as well once they have a decent food catalog. 

But for people trying to get a handle on health flair ups...this is really great and informative once you get past the 2 or 3 day learning curve of just entering your food, medicine and supplements manually and be pleasantly surprised when it has it ready to go.

36 y/o F, severe Crohn's disease, all the accompanying complications over the years. A fistula, a fissure, 6 polyps, multiple large grade 3 protruding hemorrhoids, c-diff, and now the most recent fun...SIBO. This app has it all- I can track every component of my disease process, every thing I put in my mouth including all my meds and my new strict SIBO diet, customizable symptoms such as 'anorectal pain', to differentiate from 'upper GI pain' including duration...it's just friggin awesome. One more surgery, some time on this new diet, and this app by my side...I have hope :)
Very in-depth.

If you want to log your foods at all, it's going to take forever. This app is unlike any other "health" apps in the fact that you will have to type in every nutritional fact for every type of food. They don't have a large (or any) database like MyFitness Pal or others. Sure, tracking the symptoms is a wonderful and unique feature, but it's virtually impossible to use unless you have ample time to sit and type each calorie and food in. I wish I would've known this before and not wasted my $2.99...

reviews.t: Fantastic app for food allergy/intolerance tracking
reviews.b: This app has an optimal set of features for food journaling, including sleep quantity and quality  tracker, symptoms tracker, ingredients trackers and of course food tracker. Great customization available also. Looking forward to optimization for iOS 10.

I love this app. It does everything I need it to do and more. I have gastrointestinal issues as well as anxiety. I can add symptoms to my diary and begin to isolate what could be related to food or anxiety. You can scan barcodes of foods and either they will pop right In or you add them to the public database. I can hardly think of what more this app needs.

If you have G.I. issues, or really any kind of issues that you need to keep track of, this is the app for you. It is amazingly flexible, which most apps are not. It keeps track of all kinds of things in all kinds of ways. You can make notes within the things that you were keeping track of so that you could have details of what you are detailing. I have yet to find a better app than this!
But I can't figure out how to sync with my iPad.

reviews.t: Good App-would love to see some things added
reviews.b: I like the way the app works and that it does not count calories. It would be nice to be able to track other things related to health like fiber or protein though.

reviews.t: Have user do the work for you?
reviews.b: Nice idea, but app is one big clutter. The database is very limited & needs constant adding by user even when scanning the barcode.That's not what I paid you (the developer) for when I purchased your app. Cumbersome to say the least.

This has been very helpful to me for months. It's customizable so I can add anything i need to keep track of. I highly recommend this app to others with stomach issues to keep track of everything in their daily life! Thanks mySymptoms for creating this awesome app!
Would have given five stars, but feel it needs improvement.  Larger food database would help a lot.

This app is really useful for tracking possible food sensitivities. It's one of the most comprehensive ones I've seen. However, there are a couple things that could be improved. When adding an entry, if you try to add a note, the typing area fills the entire screen to the point that you can no longer see the cursor. This makes it impossible to type... It would also be very helpful if the app would allow you to track your mood as this is often affected by food sensitivities. Otherwise, everything works great!
Excellent App! This is exactly what I needed. Keep up the good work!

This app is a must. The money is so worth it - don't even think twice. Definitely worth the download -- especially with those who are just starting out in Paleo, Celiac, PCOS etc it helps you identify triggers and symptoms to better inform your doctor how to better treat you. It's easy, it allows you to scan barcodes, it provides data and draws correlations ---- it is all the best features of the free apps combined together and then cranked up to excellence.

My stomach issues are just very complicated and I can't keep track of everything I need to in order to figure it out.  For me, this is a "Quality of Life" thing, I have very little of it.  I need to work on many issues at once while dealing with the depression this whole thing has caused.  These problems don't go away on their own.  This is the beginning of changing my whole life style.  I feel this app may really help me and I'm a stubborn case.  

This app is easy to use and only takes a few minutes.  For me, I have to track many symptoms and activity.  I also have to figure out which foods hurt or help.  When tracking food, I'm not particular about the brands and I don't enter amounts.  This probably is not the best for calorie counting. , but I can see where all this tracking may lead me to become a great food tracker someday.   

Offers great insight.  The more stuff I enter, the more I want to know and I can share accurate information with my doctor.  I want my life back.   This is a horrible problem.  I feel for anyone needing to use it.  Your not alone.
Great app. Would be even better if you could sync between apps like MyFitnessPal so you could track nutrition and symptoms without entering everything twice.

This app almost everything you need to make lasting life style changes and to become aware of your habits. We just need a place to add nutrition information. Being able to print reports for a nutrionist or doctor is wonderful.
Very nice

reviews.t: Lots of potential but terribly clunky
reviews.b: This app is in desperate need of streamlining and decluttering. To enter in a new food you have to click through a ridiculous amount of options that slows the process to the point where I'll probably stop using it for lack of convenience. Great idea poorly executed. Annoyed that I paid for this.

The mySymptoms library almost never loads properly so I end up needing to re-enter ingredients over and over. I think the app developers need to have a more expansive list of foods and a more organized/uniform way of searching for items. Without that, I wonder how accurate the results it gives you are.

Great app for me and my dietitian. She lives a bit far and so the ability to send your food diary via email is an excellent feature. 

The only small annoyance is that if there's not a food it recognizes (like those mini bell peppers) you have to create it. But it's not very difficult. Hence, the 4 stars.

I thought I was going to tackle this myself in an Excel doc. So, at least now, at the beginning - 3 days in - I don't mind having to input what's not yet in the database. It's easier after reading the user manual, so I highly recommend that. Thank you for developing this app. It's going to be a big help in finding the culprit(s).

I have celiacs and need to follow a fodmap diet to help manage my symptoms. This app is easy to use so I use it constantly. I create my reports for my dr with one click. I love it. It is well worth the price.
Great features. Easy to use.

This is EXACTLY the food journal I was searching for - easy, quick, thorough and complete to track food and symptoms.  Best way to work with my doctor to improve digestive issues while keeping me mindful of making good choices.  Thanks for offering this app!

I love that this app lets you add your own symptoms and see whether there are any correlations to what you eat. The longer you use the app the easier it becomes because your can save common recipes and their ingredients. 

2 recommendations:
Allow users to enter a start and end time to symptoms since most have a duration.
Create partnerships with companies to get them to pre-enter their product's ingredients and make it easier for users to record the pre-packaged food they eat. You could also create partnerships with cookbooks to pre-enter all those recipes and maybe even bundle the app and cookbooks together at time of sale.
I couldn't log a single meal. Ordinary item, like a wrap, are not listed. Not helpful.
Great app, helped me sort out my food issues.

I'm a newly diagnosed Celiac and this app is really helping me. I am so worried about eating enough calories (I had a feeding tube at first) as well as symptoms and possible glutenings. This app is helping me easily organize all of my information in one simple place. I will now be able to see patterns in possible foods, meds, etc that don't agree with me right now. Thank you!!
Very helpful.  Would appreciate if we could add symptoms not included on list-would be helpful if we are tracking non digestive symptoms at same time and want to do it all in one place.

I think it's been roughly 6 months since I started using this app. Initially, I tracked absolutely everything I ate/drank, in addition to everything else I still track (meds, supplements, bowels, symptoms). It helped a ton to have data handy when talking to my GI doctor about my IBS-D symptoms. Once I began taking a script for IBS-D (half a low-dose Remeron pill nightly) and my lifelong symptoms finally subsided, I quit tracking as much food/drink intake.   Thanks to this app, it's easy to see cause and effect. For example, >1/4 cup of coffee still brings on symptoms for me.
This app has been great for me. Being someone who struggles with IBS, I am able to track and narrow down the culprit of my upset stomach.
Excellent and very useful for a wide range of conditions. Could be improved by allowing for tracking of portion size.

reviews.t: Great App to keep track of your health
reviews.b: I have fibromyalgia and so far it's been a great way to keep track of my food and symptoms.

I am in the process of addressing my IBS, and having this app has made there process so much easier. I've tried food diaries before and only lasted a day or two. With the app it's been almost a month, and I'm taking more detailed notes than ever before. I do wish the food library was bigger (I generally have to add most foods myself) but other than that I'm really happy I spent the money!

reviews.t: Just what I've been looking for!
reviews.b: Very satisfied with this app so far missing some product information but overall a truly exceptional diary if you have health issues you're trying to monitor- thank you for being so thorough!!

reviews.t: Just what I was looking for!
reviews.b: I've needed a way to track not only food consumption but symptoms as well, and so far this app is exactly what I was looking for.

Are use this app to keep track of everything in my life to keep me healthy. I have a digestive condition called Crohn's or something as simple as One bad ingredient can make my day terrible. Or use this app to discover those ingredients to make my life better and easier. The only downfall is when adding foods or ingredients there is not a lot to choose from. At the same time to me that doesn't matter a whole lot because it's just as easy to look at what I'm eating and add it to the cloud so other people can use it in the future. In the end this is very helpful obviously there still work to be done

Ere is a learning curve to this app, and it does require some data entry at first. It makes sense that this is the case because the app can do a very detailed analysis to help you correlate foods that create problems. Well worth the money and time!
This AP is exactly what I was looking for to track my food symptoms. It is also very easy to use.

The foods database is utterly useless and counterintuitive. The rest of the app is decent. It needs a lot of improvements and it should have undergone a trial period prior to making it available for sale. We are essentially making it useful by using it! But had to pay for it.

This is exactly what I needed to track my food related symptoms. So much easier and more convenient Thant logging everything by hand. 
I only wish the app had a better listing of commercial foods.

Overall I'm really happy with this app. It's very comprehensive and covers a lot of health issues. The one thing I wish it had is the ability to copy and paste your entries from a higher level. This would make entering in routines a lot easier. There is also a glitch in the notes section of the symptoms. When you type in your notes you can actually see them on the screen. Again, overall this app is a fantastic aid in helping me track what I'm consuming and my over all energy and health.

Fairly easy with entry but frustrating that food entries aren't filled out for more common foods you buy and as others say people have gone in and put # vegetable/fruit instead of just fruit and those of us not tracking that indirectly have to scroll through a ton and they don't complete whole entry like 10 strawberry and strawberry instead of strawberry and fruit. Put your details in the notes if need more information or add more columns for those people please. Good but room to improve. Will see what dietician says at end of week. Also finding food a challenge. Half of what I enter not there.

I couldn't remember to do a written food diary.  This is quick & simple to do food drink meds symptoms.. Very helpful to be able to see for myself & track & remember what caused what & when.  Can't wait to print & show my doctor!  I believe she'll pass it onto many of her other - thyroid - histamine intolerant patients!

I've used this app diligently for everything I consumed and every symptom I experienced and it has yet to yield any meaningful connection between food/drink and symptoms. The ranking doesn't make any sense and the confidence levels are only high for what it's ruled out. I've figured out the causes myself, which i could've done without the app. Additionally, the .pdf isn't useful unless you're handing it to someone who's going to enter the data into a computing system.

I would give this 5 stars but the food library is inadequate. Other than that it is a great app doing just what I need to to do. Fix the food library and make it easier to add foods in and I will rank it higher
The technology is already there for this app to be great. But unfortunately the app misses the mark. $2.99 wasted.
I use this app to record everything I eat and my symptoms and I export it for my doctor. Great, comprehensive app. I've used a few and this is my favorite.

This app has met my needs perfectly. As someone who struggles with digestive issues, this app allows me to keep track of my symptoms and food intake, among other things, in order to determine what I can and cannot tolerate. I plan on showing this data to my doctor to help him determine what is wrong with me.
I'm using the app to monitor my dietary effect on my nursing infant. I log my diet and his symptoms. It works really well.
Easy to use, intuitive data entry.
Does just what I need it to. Thank you!

It is a great app. But the down part to it is that it doesn't give you the food menu like other apps do. But I would recommend it. I am currently using it to track my symptoms based on my food intake.

Recommend it!

I have only been using this for a few days, but find it very easy to input my foods, symptoms, Meds, supplements, etc. I have high hopes for the analyses once I have more days in the database. 

I do wish it was easier to put in quantities....select the food, then the quantity. I suppose one app can't do everything, but as long as I'm recording everything I eat, it would be awesome to know calories, protein, carbs and fat in my diet.

reviews.t: Saves a lot of time over the long run
reviews.b: My doctor recommended this to help me track food and symptoms while doing an elimination-challenge diet. It's quicker and easier than tracking on paper. The "public database" has some quirky and redundant entries, but still the app is very handy after a short while.
Just started to use this app. Took me a day or so to figure it out and now I'm just waiting to build up enough information to see if it could help pin point as to why I have unexplained stomach pain.

I have kept food diaries off and on for years using Notepad; Excel; OneNote; and pen and paper. None were easy to use and they definitely didn't accommodate analysis. Mainly because every day was  another opportunity to describe a symptom or food in a new way. This app provides consistency in reporting and does the analysis for me. 

Could the list of foods and other choices be cleaner? Maybe. But you have to tie down the freedom to add those items which is a different PITA. This app has an often used list which works great.
Just what I needed:)
Love this app, great for figuring out GI problems
This app has potential but it is not intuitive. I would not recommend this app to someone who has a difficult time getting around an app.

I've been having some major stomach problems and this app has been amazing at helping me keep track of all my daily activities: eating, exercise, etc., which I can use to show my doctor. It has been a great help!

reviews.t: Ginger ale is a kind of beer?
reviews.b: Promising but need breadcrumbs to help navigation and some strange priorities when it comes to including / classifying foods.

I am so glad I downloaded this app.  I am able to keep track of foods, symptoms, medicines, moods, and more.  Not only that, but I can email myself reports to print and take along to the doctor with me.  It is important to remember that correlation is not causation; that said, the data presented by this app is definitely helping me narrow down the suspects.  I have no problems recommending this app to anyone trying to figure out their food issues.
Does exactly what it's supposed to do.

I've been looking for a good app to start recording my daily food intake. Sadly this app is so cumbersome to input food. Not to mention the lack of room for details is pitiful. It's is not worth purchasing.

This is a very useful app. I left one star off because I think it needs a few tweaks.  I feel that the ability to graph and chart other things, such as the number of bowel movements in a day, water drunk in a day,  and so forth, would be very helpful.

I'm doing a low FODMAP elimination diet & purchased this app to track food & symptoms. I find it very easy to use and it has the functionality I need, including being able to generate a PDF log for my dietitian. The database can be annoying in that users choose to share really specific entries (i.e. 13 raspberries) instead of keeping those private; if I were able to make a change I'd have the generic entry (raspberries) default to the top choice when you search so you don't have to scroll through all the custom choices to find it.

This is my first week using the app. My doctor wants a detailed journal from me. I like the app but it would be great if the food part incorporated a myfitnesspal type of application. Then calories, nutrients and portions would be hugely beneficial for me and my doctor.

This app is much more in depth than it looks. It gives you only as much as you put into it though, meaning you have to spend some time adding your foods, ingredients, symptoms, notes, times, medications, and whatever else consistently to get any sort of accurate results. As for the food database, it's only as good as the users that contribute. It doesn't track calories or specific ingredients unless you take the time to input that information yourself. Really this is just for you to understand what you are putting in your body to help you get an idea of your habits. Otherwise it is great for tracking headaches, intestinal issues, or customized health problems. Absolutely recommend this app for anyone trying to track their symptoms.

reviews.t: Very Nice, but getting too cluttered
reviews.b: This app has really helped clarify my food and drink choices, and exercise habits. After only a couple of weeks of logging it's clear that some of my meal choices have been lacking in one thing or another, particularly protein, which explains why my stomach cramps right after eating sometimes. The only thing I'm really very unhappy about is that the favorites tab does not list my favorite injuries. Instead it lists everyone's entries, therefore I'm having to scroll through forever or add specific entries for why I'm using this take your app in the first place… Which is to log the foods/type of food and not the actual amount of every food. I just wish that, for instance, when I search for a food such as onions, that I don't have to see everyone else's quarter cup, half cup, 1 cup, 2 tablespoons, etc., etc., etc before finding a simple entry of "onions". This is becoming increasingly frustrating to me as I continue to use the app and more people use the app.
I love it. It easy to log my food journey

reviews.t: Great app that has helped me bunches!
reviews.b: I was just recently diagnosed with ulcerative colitis in July at only 20 and was looking for something that would help me control my symptoms as well as monitor my bowel movements and being user friendly and organized! This is a great app for anyone who has experienced any IBS or IBD symptoms because I ALWAYS have my phone on me there's no more worries about missing that quick snack I had on the run or those seemingly simple symptoms until it's too late. I like how each thing has their own category and it learns your normal foods and symptoms and bowel movements over time. I also like how it is organized and is easy to see what trends could be causing the symptoms and I like that you can print off monthly reports to show your doctor and dietician! I think it's also a nice idea that they give you samples of what kind of bowel movements you have so that you can just choose the one closest to your movement and no more wondering how much information you should be collecting for each movement! I was worried when I was diagnosed that this would control my whole life but with this app I feel like I have some control over my health again and it feels empowering!

It takes a little time to learn to use it and customize it. I primarily use it as a food journal since I don't have a lot of symptoms to need to track (I couldn't find a basic food journal that wasn't like a calorie counter - I just need to track when and what I eat!)
Once you get used to the format, it is pretty easy to customize and navigate. Having a shared food database is helpful.

I have been lactose intolerant for about a year or so and my family kept saying go to the doctor...okay I get it. But if I go what do I say without any facts. I never considered IBS-D since its very uncommon for a man to have it. So my wife suggested this app. I started using it just like it said. I have been amazed in my progress after stopping to eat the foods with a high score of problematic, the most recent of which was mustard. Now when I go to see my doctor in about a month I will have the facts and go from there.
Just one quick question. Analysis window being 24 hours. Is that the right time window?

...then you need to figure out what's irritating your gut. I've tried to keep a food intake diary on paper before, without success. This app is the solution...you always have your phone with you so there's no difficulty in recording everything you need to record.

This app is helpful for recording your food and everything, but I thought it was supposed to help you figure out what offends your stomach, and it doesn't. Maybe it just hasn't, yet, but I've had it for a while and I never see any results. At least I can show my GI Doctor the list and symptoms and everything, but I doubt they're going to want to go through it all on my phone. It'd be even better if you could somehow print the diary, and not just by screen-shotting it (because that doesn't show everything).

reviews.t: Easy to send reports to my doctor
reviews.b:
Great for tracking everything: food, sleep, headaches, bowel movements. I use this to send reports to my nutrition doctor with ease.

Could use a better calorie tracking system however.

Started a low FODMAP diet and this app has been great for tracking my symptoms in order to determine what my trigger(s) might be.  The database appears to be improving as people share what they consume.  Yes, you might have to type an item in once, but then it is there.  One suggestion for improvement would be to add "urination" to track frequency and duration. (My doctor asked for this info.). Besides, it makes sense to track output since we can track  input ("drinks") and because "bowel" is also tracked.

reviews.t: Great app to keep track of diet
reviews.b: The app makes it very easy to add all of my intake to a diary, I think that the analysis could be a little better but maybe it needs more time to record my foods and symptoms?  I really live the barcode scan feature....one of the best parts of the app!
I got this to figure out what foods were upsetting my stomach. I have a few suspects based on the app's analytics.
Extremely easy app that helps you track your food and bowel movements.
Helps me keep track of my food, exercise, sleep, supplements, and symptoms all in one! Super easy to use once you've added in your regular foods/vitamins.
I have had migraines for years and I am doing a three week elimination diet and this app is a lifesaver. Easy functionality in very well laid out.
Exporting the data is easy so you can sent details to your medical professional. Highly recommend.

If you're someone with many interrelating or not symptoms with food/other sensitivities great for charting full range- especially if you are doing this anything across apps and written notes like I have been. As other reviewers have said its a bit demanding but I don't mind that - few updates I would like them to make as they develop like being able to take photos and sync sleep apps. Haven't used the raw data yet curious for that
Extremely confusing to learn

I'm trying to figure out what foods may or may not irritate my stomach because I have chrons disease. This app makes it soooo easy for me. I only wish entering foods was a little simpler. But it isn't a big deal. Really useful, easy to use, smart.

This app has everything I need to log my food, medications, symptoms, even bowel movements!! Requires a LOT of food and medication ingredients input, but hopefully with the help of the community a larger database can be built. Contacting the developers to confirm.
This makes keeping a food journal so insanely easy. I just wish I would've found it sooner!

I was looking for a way to track my food intake and medication compared to my health and symptoms and this is the magic bullet. The reporting side needs a little polishing but there is some great potential for diagnostics here. 
It's only as good as you are though. 
It works best when all the details are logged, although that is sometimes difficult. To get started I just added "regular supplements" but now I'm going back in to record each supplement and dosage
Much easier to enter and categorize than anything I've ever used.  I've only been using it a few days so I haven't used the correlation capability yet, but I love where this app is heading.
For the obsessive, or genuinely perplexed regarding causation of symptoms,  this is brilliant.

reviews.t: Few clicks away from being perfect
reviews.b: It would be better if there was a way of selecting the same meal you had the day before by just one click instead of having to enter in all the ingredients over and over. Most people eat similarly everyday. Also, we can use easier ways to select time without having to go through multiple screens.

I have IBS and while I had been tracking my eating and symptoms with Google Forms for well over a year, I had no quick way of analyzing the data I had collected. This app makes it very easy to track and analyze my symptoms and eating habits and correlate the two. You can also export your data to back it up which is a really nice addition. The app even gracefully handles changes in time zone which was an unexpected surprise. The exported data is in an SQLite format which is awesome if you're a programmer and want to tinker with it. I definitely have some feature requests to submit with them but their support team seems very responsive and caring.

reviews.t: Very Helpful! Love this app. Kudos to the creators 😊
reviews.b:
I am on a special diet due to an a medical condition. It requires me to be very watchful on what I eat. This app helps a lot if you need to keep track of your food related/stress related symptoms.

Suggestions:
Medications can also include details as dosage. 
 
So far everything is perfect!!!

Great app! I'm so glad to have found it. It tracks easily and has everything I need - might be good to add 'fever' to symptoms, but other than that, it's been so helpful. I figured out some triggers within a short timeframe when I could track them.

reviews.t: It has no idea what French fries are...
reviews.b: Also the interface is pretty needlessly cumbersome

I am very grateful to have found this app! It is easy to use and has been able to be adapted to meet my own needs. I needed it to record a variety of symptoms that are not in their list, but it was easy to delete theirs and add an endless amount of different random symptoms I'm experiencing. I also love that you can state the duration, rate your symptoms, change the time something happened like if you forgot a detail and need to add it (even to yesterday's) and you can add notes to clarify something as well. My only suggestion to make this fit my needs Beyer would be to add details about nutrients, vitamins, and minerals. I'm not recording for food allergies or irritants. I'm looking for a much deeper analysis of potassium fluctuations in relation to my symptoms. I highly recommend this app. It is truly well done!!

reviews.t: A much needed app with some room for improvement
reviews.b: I have faith in this app, despite the high upfront investment in quality database entries, as other reviewers have mentioned. I’d also love a CSV export of my food log so that I can compare my food intake to data I track in other sources.
Helpful for tracking headache triggers.

Great for journaling. It could use an add function to things such as categories and symptoms. Not a lot in the cloud database but that leaves me to put in exactly what I've had and is there for the future. Overall I'm pleased and will continue to use this app.

The app takes a bit of learning. It was mostly intuitive for me but my sister's family was completely frustrated. I find myself pushing the wrong buttons a lot and being asked over and over if i want to add a food. I do like that it has learned some of my foods and has those pretty readily available. I find that the food category confuses my analysis and many items get lumped into a category like fruit which doesn't do me a lot of good because i eat some kind of fruit every day. I am very appreciative of what you have created. As always there are things you can change as you understand needs. The app can be very helpful so thank you, I need desperately to be able to identify patterns that are affecting my health.
I have found it helpful and easy to use. Wish I could store the data in iCloud so I could sync between devices. As it is, I only have to remember to only log data on my phone.
I have found this app to give me just what I needed to track what I eat and how I am feeling. I have stomach problems and this app gives me the tools to monitor what I eat and my symptoms.
Lots of features I still haven't been able to use. Great app!

After two years of un-diagnosed abdominal pain, keeping a food diary was my next step. This app makes it so much easier than a hand-written diary and I like that it's specifically geared towards tracking ingredients and symptoms as compared to other food diary apps, which are more geared towards counting calories. That being said, there could be some improvements and ditto to what some other reviews have said about the food database (like the review by Ealfieri).

Here are some of the things I like:
1. The ease at adding events, symptoms, and food at specific times. It even lets you track how severe the symptoms are and add notes to each event.
2. The way it saves your own recipes so you don't have to re-enter each time. Entering recipes with common whole ingredients is fairly quick and easy.
3. The way it saves foods you eat regularly at the top of your list to speed up the process.
4. The ability to create a PDF of your diary that you could give to a doctor.

Here are some things I don't like:
1. It allows users to share ingredients they've added with other users in the general database, which in theory is a good idea but in practice it has really muddled up the list of ingredients. For example, there are many duplicate ingredients in the database, which could mess up your results if you choose one "corn" one time and another "corn" another time. There are also too many really specific items listed in the general database - for example "2 french fries" or "breakfast burrito" (with specific ingredients that probably don't match the burrito you're eating). 
2. It is very tedious to add all the ingredients to pre-packaged food, especially if it's something you might not eat on a regular basis. The app has a bar code scanner but I was surprised that almost nothing was already in the database.

Some suggestions: 
1. Have a better pre-set database of your common basic ingredients. Maybe even code these a different color to differentiate them from items other users have added.
2. Only allow users to share information for items with a bar code. If someone went to the trouble of entering all the ingredients for Nacho Cheese Doritos, then it would be nice to collaborate and the bar codes keep it specific enough that you wouldn't be mucking up the entire database. We don't need 15 "cookies" with no useable info. 
3. At the very least, add a warning if someone is about to add an ingredient that already exists to avoid duplicates.

I should also note that I've been using the app for about 2 months and have not been able to pinpoint what is causing my symptoms. It's possible that I just need more data but I also wonder if this is because so many of the ingredients are not categorized well (i.e. dairy, grains, etc), duplicated, or too specific. I have not had the time to enter everything to the amount of detail necessary since that would be extremely time consuming. I think I would need to completely avoid using the common database for truly accurate results. 

If all you're needing is a good food diary, this app is great but the analysis portion needs improvement.

It should be listed as its name, and as a subcategory of squash. Super annoying to just have to pull up the lists I think it’s listed in and scroll around until I find it). It also doesn’t include sugar alcohols and herbal/extracted sweeteners that are popular and/or becoming popular with the ketogenic diet (as well as Candida protocol, which has some overlap with the low-FODMAP and keto diet). What is nice is it gives you amounts that are safe or what you should limit it to, which I think is helpful. And when you click on the ones high in FODMAPs, it specifies which kind of FODMAP it’s high in. reviews.t: Needs a “Sort by Low FODMAP” filter
reviews.b:
It’s really frustrating to try to find Low FODMAP foods when they’re surrounded by all the foods I CANT HAVE (e.g. Medium and High FODMAP foods). 

While it’s nice to know what are and aren’t Low FODMAP foods, I also just need a filter that shows me only Low FODMAP foods. I want the full list of Low FODMAP foods in alphabetical order so that I can create a shopping list based on the ingredients I’m already familiar with. In other words, I’ve seen a lot of Ingredients on these Low FODMAP lists that are foods I’ve either never heard of or have no idea where (if at all) I could purchase them. And yes, I have seen that this app has a Low FODMAP food delivery service. However, I don’t have a ton of money right now to go blowing it on an expensive 3-meals-per-day delivery service. 

Long story short, it’s very discouraging to open this app and see that the overwhelming majority of foods I’m familiar with are foods I can’t have. That’s like trying to create a shopping list by almost solely listing off the things you CAN’T have. 

“Alright, Honey, what’s the list like today?”

“Well, Daryl, we can’t have ice cream or dairy. We also can’t have raspberries or wheat. Oh and no honey, ‘Honey’! Did you see what I did there?”

“I saw,” Daryl chuckled. “What else can’t we have?”

“Pretty much every fruit known to mankind,” Lisa droned on, “except some hyper specific ones, but it’s almost impossible to find those on the app or in reality.” 

“Oh look!” Lisa points to her phone’s screen, “Something we CAN have: brown rice!”

“Brown rice upsets my stomach, remember?” Daryl said.

reviews.t: Hot mess of an app. Buy the real one.

I’ve used this app twice for a FODMAP diet. IMO, after using this to eat with for 3 months, it’s more trouble than it’s worth. On the surface it seems helpful, but it’s missing crucial info to make it helpful to people living with this diet. 

1) Data is disorganized, missing, or needs editing. Sometimes there are multiple similar entries for the same foods. Just look at the oatmeal section if you don’t believe me. Or “coconut milk with insulin”- whatever that is supposed to be. Lots of foods are missing, too- inulin, pectin, celery powder, grape juice concentrate, raisin juice, gooseberries, etc. 

2) Only the low ranges of “safe” foods are listed and their FODMAP categories aren’t listed (like the “unsafe” foods). The problem is that you can stack “safe” foods of the same type and trigger a reaction by eating too many of that type at the same time. How much of a safe food is too much?? Which foods can be combined safely?? This app does not help with that. 

3) Also, the high fodmap foods don’t have a safe amount listed. I don’t need 8 Oz of OJ to make a marinade, I need like a few spoonfuls. So how much OJ is a safe amount? Why is the low range not provided? 

Save yourself the trouble and cough up the $8.

reviews.t: Add Filter for Reintroduction Phase by Group
reviews.b: I have been using this app for a few weeks and overall find it generally pretty quick and helpful in everyday lifestyle things like shopping and looking up recipe ingredients for cooking at home.  In a few weeks I will be starting my reintroduction phase and I can’t seem to find a way to search or sort by the FODMAP groups.  It would be great to have that feature for example if I started to reintroduce the “F- fermentable” group for a week or maybe the “O- oligosaccahrides”, it would be so helpful to know all the foods that fall in that category because it may not be so intuitive as say generally knowing that onions, apples, broccoli, watermelon, certain cheeses and breads etc are high fodmaps (if I don’t know which FODMAP group they fall into).  So maybe in an updated version there could be both the red, green, yellow color and then next to it also the acronym letters for FODMAP and a filter feature for people who are in elimination and re-introduction phases, or simply trying to figure out which groups cause them problems.  Thank you.

I had no idea how intuitive this app is going to be. I’m using it to track my meals and how I feel/react after meals. I love that you can share your progress and results with team members who may be working with you on your journey. I love that you can simply take a picture of your food, it gets captured with a timestamp , instead of having to write down everything you eat. It all shows neatly in the timeline. I’m starting to use this instead of my other micro nutrient tracking app, The other app has its purpose but this is faster and better for basic food allergy tracking. Love the centralize nature of it and how I can add comments and thoughts after each event. 

My only wish is that there was a way to export the data to PDF or google calendar to share with people who do not have the app.
Wish it had restaurant items such as Starbucks.

There are a lot of herbs not on here. I couldn't find dandelion or chicory ROOT, only leaf. Schizandra berry didn't show up. For some reason fennel seed is low but fennel tea is high. I’ve tried searching a number of other herbs and nothing is coming up. Makes herbal tea drinking really hard. (As for weak teas, if brewed weakly you don’t get any benefit from the herbs unless they steep at least 5-10 min).

This is very helpful in navigating a new world of sensitivities I’m experiencing while recovering from c. diff. I just wish there were a little more explanation about the way the food rating system works. It was a little confusing the first time I used it. Otherwise, indispensable tool!
Finding out I had IBS was concerning, this APP is quick and helpful!
Excellent app for people following FODMAP.  Has a listing of food, a diary, and quiz
a super useful app! I’m new to it but it’s helped me a lot!

Why is broccoli low, but the stalk is high and the head is low? Wouldn’t that make broccoli medium? I DONT UNDERSTAND. 
And can you pleeeeaaaaaase test Kimchi? Also: please make an ABSOLUTELY DONT EAT list??
This is the best!  I’m able to quickly and easily check foods that I have to avoid. Just enter the food and the FODMAP level is there along with the sugar that is produced when you eat it. Fantastic!
This is a pretty good app but anytime I search for certain foods, like certain seed or nuts or veggies, it can find anything. Consider expanding the number of searchable foods

Just type in food to get the answer to low, medium or high FODMAP. Also has flashcard game where you guess's which foods have low, medium or high levels which is an entertaining way to learn. Does not have 100% of every food but I found more than enough foods I like to eat that will give me a nutritious start on this lifestyle
I was recently diagnosed with IBS-C and this app is my go to to find foods I can actually eat. Very helpful and WOW it’s free.

I like this app pretty well and I would rate it higher, but when I am logging a meal from a previous day it always goes to the day that I am actually logging the meal. That’s pretty frustrating. There’s also a few items missing from the list, Matcha tea for one. So if these things were fixed I would rate it much higher
Love this app, it tells me everything I want to know
This is not the monash university app! What is up?

Been using this app for months now. It’s mostly good but at times my husband would still have bad “IBS” days. We figured it was normal, you never know w IBS. 

However, today he had Brussel sprouts and a blueberry smoothie in  in the morning  which are on the app as low (Not even medium). Well, he had a crazy bad IBS episode. 

We follow this app like the Bible. Well I google blueberries and it states to be careful with the amount mostly in smoothies. And what about Brussel sprouts???? HIGH. They’re a High FodMap

This is the whole purpose of this app. I’m disappointed that it’s “mostly” good but not 100% accurate. 

I recommend the Monash University app which is also called FODMAP. But make sure it’s the real one. It’s $8 dollars but it’s so worth it. Doesn’t seem to have erroneous information like this app. 

So sad but can’t afford to have these IBS nightmares.  

Now I wonder if those bad IBS episodes in the past were triggered by foods that are mistakenly labeled on this app. Very disappointing

I just want to say a HUGE thank you to the creator/s of this app. I’ve been trying to juggle so many moving parts of my dietary issues since February, but this is the first time it’s felt manageable. The app is so intuitive and I can’t tell you how incredible it is to be able to store recipes, meal plans, AND keep a good diary all in one place. It seems ridiculous that on top of all that, I get notes of encouragement throughout the day! It’s apparent to me that this was born from good people who truly have the desire to help others. I’m amazed and grateful!
the app icon to this app is too good. it doesn’t make sense

reviews.t: I have never seen a medical app like this before!
reviews.b: This app is amazing! From the amazing food logging features to the little rewards and memes they send, this makes app makes an extremely hard diet feel easy

Lots of great information on this app. I would like to see a version that I can use to scan items while I am shopping at the grocery store. It would eliminate a lot of the guess work.

reviews.t: Great way to log a diet
reviews.b: This app is great for looking up items and logging a diary. Like the positive affirmation too

What a great app! Makes it easier to figure out what I can safely eat!
Thanks!

reviews.t: Great app! So many hidden features
reviews.b:
I just got diagnosed with IBS and I’m getting a colonoscopy next month. I’m glad I found this app i originally downloaded it for the fodmap section but the diary was a pleasant surprise. 

One thing I wanted to add is having more variety of food. I am Asian so I like to eat more Asian style food and there isn’t a lot of that listed here.

Other than that small complaint this is a great app! So happy it’s free for everyone!!!!!

reviews.b:

Is it possible for an option to show all foods in the lookup screen by default and have the filter only show the foods I need to avoid based on my filter settings? No other app does this and it would make things so much easier! Thanks!

If I close the app or it background times out, the settings reset! This is very annoying. If that got fixed, this app would be perfect and I'll change this to a 5 star review.
I can quickly search any food I’m thinking of eating. I’m new to this IBS thing so I’m really having to be aware of what I eat.

This is awesome! 
This is exactly what we need, I'm glad I found it. In some of the notes and thoughts I'm putting in added/extra details that I think may be helpful. I think there needs to be a poop journal also unless I'm missing something.
Food, exercise, encouragement (love it, what an amazing idea), goals, connect with others like a dietician or invite someone you know.
I wish I could check my heart rate. Maybe I'll take it myself?
Coaching would be nice. Like financial goals and getting to bed goals.
Meal planning is probably one of the hardest because I'm so exhausted and sick (that's why I have this app right?) healthy food is sooooo expensive! 
Hmmm, well anyways, hope this much helps a bit.

I’ve been trying out different fodmap apps today. This one is far different and much more useful to me than the others that I have tried.  The learning game, the personalized tracking information, and the quick data lookup are all very helpful to me at this stage of learning how to eat low fodmap.

The app seems limited on foods, types of foods, and brands.  I don’t have lots of money to buy specialty foods but due to its limited food selection I don’t know how well it will suite me.  For example, I tried looking up oatmeal but the only options in the app were organic and gluten free.  I tried looking up other foods as well like grits, breakfast bars, and some name brand items and they weren’t found.
It’s about time somebody build a full-scale comprehensive app that helps me manage this crazy diet. Thank you so much! Great work!
My was just placed on a Low FODMAP diet and this super-easy to use app makes cooking for him a lot easier.
I love this app! All the foods I thought were good for me turned out to be not good for my gut!

This app makes it so much easier to make quick food choices cuz I haven’t memorized the whole FODMAP list. It also tells you low, medium and high concentrations so I can choose to eat a little of the medium foods and still be OK.

This is a great tool to help you quickly navigate food choices. I can’t even imagine going through this process without it. It is BETTER than the expensive alternative and is significantly more streamlined. With that said, many of the items I attempt to look up are not listed (on any of the app options). Hopefully, as time goes on the list will be expanded.

reviews.t: Cannot find several of the items
reviews.b: I could not find hemp seed, water Kefir or raw goat Kefir
A MUST! Thanks! This app is the almost perfect addition to my “game “ plan! It’s great on my phone..so helpful to be able to look up a particular food to see if it’s acceptable!

FollwIng a FODMAP diet can be daunting. But this app makes it super easy to make the right choices. I also appreciate the food and stool logs. This helps me be more aware of my choices and provides vital information for how I’m feeling and what may have triggered a reaction. I’m sure it will be very helpful in my next doctors appointment. I wonder if there is a “download logs feature” to make it easy to share with healthcare professionals

Quick. Easy. And like the "quiz" function.  
Best one so far
The fodmap game is helping me actually learn which foods I can eat, it's great.

And the reason you don’t have this info is because it’s protected by the IP of Monash who actually spent the hundreds of thousands of dollars to test the foods. And why their app is the only accurate app on the market.

I also want to really know some of these myself and that's where the learning mode comes in. With minimal time, you get to really learn. Avocado is high? Come on..... ;)

This app changed my life and helped me restore my health. I’m 20 years old, and a few months ago, I could not digest more than a couple ounces of protein at a time. I never felt well- I suffered from severe acid reflux, bloating, gas, constipation, and hair loss, and the anxiety surrounding food ruled my life. After a few months on the low FODMAP diet, all my digestion issues have resolved, and I feel so much better and happier. This app makes it possible for me to quickly and confidentially make the right choices and feel well day to day. The information about FODMAPs varies from source to source and is often inaccurate, but I have found that this app is always accurate and reliable. Thank you for developing this guide and helping IBS sufferers like me reclaim their lives.

Otherwise it’s a good app and the ads are actually helpful for us IBS (I think, though I’m going to get tested for IBD) sufferers.

For unknown reasons I developed “adult-onset-allergies” to dozens of foods, vegetation, etc. From getting allergy shots to developing SIBO (small intestinal hydrogen issues) my ability to eat anything has become so complicated! All my life I’ve rarely eaten anything “processed” or sugar (only Stevia and fresh meats, veggies & fruit). This APP” has become my guide from just shopping in supermarkets to dining in restaurants. I just returned from Europe where restaurateurs - and waiters - are totally in tune with ingredients and happy to help. It’s getting a bit better here, but is still slow to catch up. 
When in doubt, CHECK THIS APP! Right at the table or in the market. It’s saved me physical pain from digestive issues and sleepless nights.

First, I wish there were more ingredients listed since sometimes I want to look up something I see on a label, but 90% of the time the app has what I’m looking for.  Second, I wish I could tag a food/ingredient into a “good” and “bad” bucket to help me track what I’m finding as an irritant and what I’m not.

This app is very helpful when stating portion size for each item simply by tapping on it. This way, a person can know how much is considered an average portion and that a smaller portion of a certain food may not cause adverse effects. The app also breaks down the components that can cause possible bad reactions in each item so a person might learn which components they are most sensitive to. I like the three color system for this and for each food item in general. I’m glad the developer will continue to add more food choices as reliable information about them becomes available.

Speedy way to look up FODMAP levels. 

Suggestions:

1.) Allow users to add their own entries to their list. For example, crab is not listed. A quick google search shows that crab is low FODMAP. Users should then be able to create a crab entry in their app. This would also apply for foods that contain lots of ingredients. For example, a user might want to record a specific brand/flavor of bread that is reliably low FODMAP. 

2.) An icon that shows the color status is dependent on serving size. For example, wheat pasta shows as red but if you click it, it shows that a half cup is green but a whole cup is red.

Good app, but I wish I knew the basis of their claims as so many different sources conflict. Also wish there were more foods listed
Excellent App!!!!
This site is EXTREMELY helpful in showing what’s appropriate to eat and what is detrimental
Very helpful. Hopefully in the future more foods will be added.

I love this app. It is so helpful and to use!
I only wish that it included more. I’d love more spices and liquors on here so I know how I can cook and socialize safely. 

Thank you!
I hope they add more foods. What would be great would be if you could scan a package’s bar code and a numerical value would come up.
This a good resource but I find it. We limited in the foods listed.
Very convenient to have at my fingertips when I am food shopping.

Revised. Thank you for the reply I see where I confused the 2. I need to play with this to provide a proper review. I updated this to remove my false rating.

How can you list broccoli as green (head, stalk & whole) & also red?

reviews.t: Nearly as good as Monash University app
reviews.b: It sources the same data as the Monash App. While easier to lookup foods than Monash app, it does not list which fodmap category restricted green foods fall under. (Green foods where portion sizes are not unlimited.)

reviews.t: It does what I need mostly
reviews.b: I like that this app tells you servings of FODMAPS. That helps me a ton. However, I wish it had more food choices and that it was easier to look up a specific item. Also some conflicting information such as searching for soy milk. One says it’s high and the other says low depending on how you searched for it. I do like having a quick reference though and it saves me from buying the $8 app.

Developer improved scrolling. Upper right provides options for searching - advise using it. Hey developer, if you make the choice in upper right bolder, people will notice it more readily. Your improvement works well. Thanks.
Should change from stop light to percentages/concentration of fodmaps.

This could be so much more useful. The light system doesn’t say how much of the fodmap types are in how many grams of food, so it is difficult to determine how foods stack together in one meal. This would be so much better if you could build your own recipes to check the sum total  fodmaps. Developers, please check out MacroFactor for an example of how nice this would be for users! Also, I do all my nutrition stuff in grams and I don’t see a way to switch from oz to grams in the app. Frustrating.

reviews.t: Confusing app without clear ways to use it
reviews.b: Hi.  I just modified my review to 3 stars from 1.  I’ve gotten to know the app a bit  better ( still think it’s a bit confusing for a  newbie), and am finding that the daily log is my favorite feature in that I can keep a clear record of food intake “outgo”🤭and symptoms in between as they do or do not arise.  i have also download ed and made several of the recipes, and though they’re laid out in terms of weight, it’s easy enough to translate into cups.  I still feel it’s a bit too heavily weighted with hints to use the food prep service “Modify Health” which would be great, but not everyone can afford such. I would love to see a couple weeks of sample meal plans and maybe another dozen or so more recipes on the app, a few more for each type of meal listed.  Basically I need to look on lists to see if various this and that's are green, yellow or red lit?  I had thought with a paid app, that I would be getting listed out meal plans to follow, in addition to the red, yellow, green light system.

reviews.t: Only for the highly motivated, data nerds willing to put in effort
reviews.b:
While this app is extremely useful at looking up individual foods, it is very much less useful for meal planning unless you are willing to expend considerable time and effort figuring out the total fodmap rating for a meal yourself.  

I ended up utilizing a (privacy-protecting) AI program to plan low fodmap meals instead.  (Beware of AI's privacy invasion.) 

Maybe don't waste your money?
Just bought the app and it can’t even properly sort products by filtering for products in your own country. Very frustrated and wish I wouldn’t have bought this

reviews.t: They change the privacy policy after you pay/sign up
reviews.b: They changed the privacy policy for US and it’s not very functional/applicable for US. I do not recommend. Very disappointing

I wish they’d offer a free trial first so I could see that this is not a terribly user friendly app. Common words don’t come up by typing a few letters and you have to type the entire thing or it’s showing you random items unrelated to what you’re searching. I’d love a refund. I won’t be using this.

The app is just the extended version of the web site with searchable feature on a limited tested food. The challenge is still thousand of other products out there that i will have to second guess or through trial and error. Pricing is not great based on provided contents. The gluten free app was cheaper with better functionality and community base evaluation on eating out choices. The university staff needs to hurry up with the upgrade; unless this is only an attempt to recover the research costs. Not a problem there, but i think i would have to find the not so official tool to manage my condition.
It’s better to just get a diary booklet and fill it out yourself. This does not help me one bit.

Charged me without my consent. Did not even put my credit card info in but it still charged me $8.49. Maybe it was in a germs and conditions but when I checked the app to cancel that I could not find a subscription area. Not even that helpful with recipes either.

iPhone 14 Pro, updated. 
*In filtering, the sides of the screen are cut off. On the left, I see what is likely the word lactose or fructose etc, but all I see are the last two letters.  On the right, I see part of an unhappy face. 
* When searching ingredients, whether from the category of food or from the certified list, most returns are recipes or premade products that contain that food.
*There doesn't appear a category for diabetics or allergies, celiac, so many foods are presented when the user knows they can't have it. 

It's pretty basic and not what I expected. A trial period before buying would have been useful. I don't think I'll be using this app much.
I use this every day for every meal and have for a few years now.

I’m very disappointed in this app. The food search (which seems to be its primary use) feels poorly designed and like an ad for companies that have paid to be included. Half of the things I pull up are specific brand names, all of which are green (so ok to eat). For example, I searched rice cereal: Rice Krispies are green, but the generic puffed rice cereal is yellow (and yes, I understand they might use different sweeteners, but it still feels like an ad when the name brand is promoted like that). Additionally, specific home delivery meal kits keep showing up when I just search for a vegetable, cluttering everything up and making it hard to use. The serving size of items is also misleading. A fruit might be marked as green but when you look at the serving sizes, it will say 2.1 oz is green but 2.3 oz is yellow and 3 oz is red, and maybe the people who made this app have never eaten fruit before, but there is very little difference in a 2.1 oz serving of fruit and a 3 oz serving of fruit.

I’ve had IBS all my life and found out about the low FODMAP elimination diet by my GI doctor as an adult. I downloaded this years ago and I have found out some of my intolerances that I didn’t know. When I was little I was always sick to my stomach and had a lot of pain and cramping. Didn’t know my intolerance to lactose. Back then they diagnosed me with IBS but blamed it on stress. Nobody did anything for me. My mom took me doctor to doctor and nothing. Not even a mention of an antacid for my reflux. You guys have done amazing work and I’m so thankful for you. This is an amazing app studied by amazing professors and students. If there was one thing I could add to the app is a filter that I could set to my intolerance group and see all the food from all the different groups together. Instead I have to search each item and take a pen and paper and write down all the intolerances in that group!! That would make this app so much better for me at least!! Thank you for your great work.

I am not a chef, nor can I read the creators of this app’s minds while cooking. While making a recipe like the chicken risotto, it tells you to sauté the vegetables all the way on high in the beginning. And then proceeds to tell you everything else you need to add. Not once does it tell you to reduce the heat. So here I am burning the living you know what out of this entire dish and now it’s disgusting and I wasted my money. And my kitchen is a burnt mess on top of it. I do not know how to cook anything without detailed instructions. Not telling when to reduce heat, or simmer, that’s a huge problem. Should have been a disclaimer about the level of cooking knowledge required for this app.

Been using this app for a few days and I’m disappointed to say the least. There are not many recipe options and the search function is extremely dated and has very few brands and specifics. The app description also states that there is a reintroduction guide but this was also hard to navigate and isn’t much of a guide. I am grateful for the research and I’m sure some of the cost of the app goes to funding but unfortunately as the consumer if we have to use apps behind paywalls there are much better ones for the same purpose.

This app, a registered dietician, and 6 months of focused work allowed me to find my 2 triggers (of 6) and reduced IBSD symptoms by 90%.   Prior to this, not a single one of my US MDs, not even the gastro, gave me any real instruction on how to do the low fodmap elimination process.  They deprived me of any opportunity for recovery, through ten YEARS of soiling myself at work.  I'm grateful Australians invested in this evidence based practice.   Get a dietician and this ten dollar app - it's priceless.

reviews.t: Great app, please add option to Import Diary or sync data
reviews.b:
This app is pretty great. I used it to do an elimination diet, and afterwards I have been using it to track my diet. It’s not perfect, there are bugs sometimes, and I wish it would function better sometimes, but I’m still glad I bought this app and it use daily.

I really wish there was a way to input diary data from my phone when I am out, and have it sync with my ipad, where the majority of the database is stored. It is extremely time consuming to transfer the data manually. Or at least, if there was a way to export and IMPORT the diary, that would work too and avoid the problem with using cloud data. I would definitely pay extra for the option to just sync data in the cloud though!

I can look up online what foods are high FODMAP which is the only thing this app does well. I wanted a meal plan for elimination. You get recipes but no plan. It has a start the diet button but it’s more literature. There’s no support while you’re on the diet. There’s no dietitians in my area and I can look that up on their free website. The diary could be nice if it helped you along the way. It’s basically a place to take notes without any prompts to know why you’re logging what. I want my $7.99 back.

I wish there was a better way the app can be used to guide the reintroduction. If the diary entries only have specific foods to track, it would be better to then have a plan that actually helps you reintroduce these foods. 

Also there may be some specific food intolerances in certain foods that should also be allowed to track. I don’t really understand why you can’t add any food item to your diary. From the food lookup you can only add a personal note, where does this get centralized? Why can’t you add the diary entry from here? 

Overall great information, but the flows could really be improved. I’m resorting to tracking this stuff in a notes app just because I can’t enter in specific food items in the diary.

reviews.t: Super helpful! Many ways to improve!
reviews.b:
I really appreciate this app and feel it is super worth it for the diary function and cross examination of foods. The concept is unique and insanely helpful. It could use a lot of work in terms of streamlining, helping us understand data, and being more accommodating/accurate. I’ll list some of my observations below and would always be happy to give ux/ui feedback in the future via email. 

-Female health: the female body is very different than the male body. Depending k my cycle, I need completely different things, have higher malabsorption rates, and different sets of motility symptoms. Incorporating this would be a game changer and differentiate you from other sources
-Data analysis: it would be great to be able to cross compare symptoms, and have an analysis drawn by the app from different foods. Also, this would be made much easier by adding a drop down feature for choosing food in meals, instead of just writing it. 
-The landing page is awkward, could use some testing and redesign to know what users need quickly in the service flow 
-Add widgets for iPhone!

So this app could so easily be fixed I want to scream. It’s like whoever made it never went grocery shopping. You know what would be fantastic? Make a section in filtering for the app of what you CANNOT eat when you’ve know which carbs your sensitive too.
