I started using Cara to track my meals and symptoms since I started having a lot of stomach issues. It’s a great app and super easy to use. It helps me track everything I need and analyze what could be causing certain problems in my diet. Highly recommended!

I have been consistently tracking for a while now and the suggestions for what food is causing my bad days are inaccurate. Also I had a 25 day streak of tracking. When I went to put in my 26th day of tracking it reset saying I had missed a day of tracking even though my calendar shows no missed days of documenting.

I’ve been tracking symptoms, poop, food and it’s really a good app for my UC.
It has everything that I need to keep a track of my body. I highly recommend this app if you have colitis or any gastroentestinal problem to keep track of everything.
It’s so user friendly, and makes logging my symptoms and diet so easy and convenient.
The Cara App has helped me control my IBS better & to tell my doctor when there’s a problem. Thank you so much for the Cara App. I just love it.

Cara really makes tracking my flares, symptoms, & trigger foods easy. The only thing that would make it better would be if it had a good database (like how Fitbit does). Other than that this app has been a huge help!

I have Crohn’s disease and so far this has been a fascinating tool to track so many valuable aspect of my diet and digestion and exercise.  Eager to see what is coming in the announced updates soon.  Hoping for a good scanning option like they use for medications, works well.  Also, would like to see incorporation of weight tracking, not just targeted at weight loss but truly historical tracking of weight gain and loss.  This is still a very robust app for keeping track of the wide variety of variables that contribute to everyone’s overall well being.  Keep up the great work here!

reviews.t: What you see is not what you will get
reviews.b:
I just downloaded this. I got a message that says data correlation will not be available due to an upcoming update. Also, you have to create an online account to move your data to the new update. So all that health data you were able to keep to yourself has to be shared with them or you lose it all. What do you get in return? ‘New recipes headed your way!’ Like I need more recipes or have any trouble finding them. 

Sounds like a data grab to push tailored (sponsored) content to you. 

Glad I had only entered one data point in what should have been a rare promising health app.
This app has been so helpful tracking allergies and intolerances to help me understand my body better.

I started using this app a month ago and already I’ve figured out that I seem to have more problems with certain types of food. It’s fairly using to use and add symptoms and food. I like that you can take pictures of food if you don’t have time to add in all the ingredients right then.
This app does exactly what I need it to for gathering a food journal for my dietician. And it is easy to use, easy on the eyes!

The day I downloaded this app was the day after I had an emergency appendectomy. It’s been an easy way for me to pay attention and focus into my gut health as well as how my workouts, stress, etc could affect my digestion. I also love how it’s not a calorie counter. Yeah putting the food in is a little tedious but it’s important if you’re trying to pay attention to how your body feel after eating and doing certain things. I’m 2 weeks post op and 14-days strong using this app. My body feels better each and every day and I know as I utilize this app more and more it’ll do well I’m showing what my tummy likes and dislikes more effectively. It keeps me mindful.

reviews.t: Great tracking for IBD flare up
reviews.b: Great tool to track symptoms, medicines and food when going through a flare up and learning what are my trigger foods. Wish there was more nutritional factors on the app because otherwise I would have to log my food in another app (but really who has time for that!)
It keeps sending my notifications in German. I dont speak German. They say important. Please help.

It’s been great for me and a wonderful way to track the symptoms of my IBS, but now the app keeps crashing whenever I try to log anything. I know we keep getting notifications of a new update coming up, but something needs to be done about this crashing issue.
I’m on day 11 of tracking and I still can’t see my best and worst foods. Don’t download.
This app is awesome. Not only does it help me keep track of my symptoms, but I find that I’m eating better since keeping track of what I eat.
Using Cara has not only helped me track a wide range of symptoms, but also remember to take my meds, and figure out long-term trends. My doctor was impressed with the app too.

reviews.t: Cara is good for food tracking and more
reviews.b: This is the first app I have found that allows me to track food and symptoms. I didn’t realize how much I needed that. It is a very valuable resource for me as I am Trying to find foods in my diet that bother me.
This is the most efficient way I have found to track food/sleep/workouts to identify patterns that trigger symptoms. Highly recommend for anyone looking to start or improve on their food diary.
Does a good job of keeping track of my food and many, many symptoms

reviews.t: App is promising but some lacking functionality
reviews.b:
I have IBS and downloaded this based on a friend's recommendation. The amount of data and insights is really great along with the kinds of information you can track (seems quite specific to digestion issues which is great.) The app is easy to use, is ad-free, and has a nice UI. There are a few changes I'd like to suggest:

- integration with MyFitnessPal so I can reduce effort and avoid inputting my food twice. I like to track my nutrition info and make note of amounts of food I am eating per meal as opposed to just the ingredient name
- expanded list of foods/ingredients available
- import ingredient lists from store-bought food

reviews.t: Also good for Bile Acid Malabsorption
reviews.b: I know this is a popular app for IBS, but I have Bile Acid Malabsorption and use this religiously. Highly recommended, this app is my lifeline for tracking.
I recently got diagnosed with Celiacs, and this app has been a lifesaver for me!! So grateful to the people who make this great resource free!!
Good for tracking but not sure on the analytics piece as to truly identifying what foods were best on what days etc and worst foods and how that ties into symptoms.

reviews.t: the most functional and helpful app out there
reviews.b: love this app so much. started using it when i found out what my stomach problems were (i have IBS). i use this app ritually it’s the best tool ever!
Cara is everything I needed in one app. It tracks all my necessary information for my doctor and myself.  It’s amazing and it’s pointing symptoms that I didn’t realize.

I’ve had some digestive issues and am trying to track my symptoms and triggers. This app has been a great help so far. I’ve been using it for about a week and have an appointment with a GI Dr. in about two more weeks. I am hoping to use this info then.
Great help with IBS symptoms. Easy to use and thorough.
Loving the ease of use, and the correlations between food and symptoms has been a huge help in figuring out what to avoid

I get various pains related to what I eat, but not a known ailment. One of the reasons I chose Cara over other options is the ability to correlate symptoms with food the day before rather than just the same day.

Two things I’d like to see: 1) sometimes my worst symptoms are 36 to 48 hours after eating something. I’d love to look at foods two days before. (Possibly even 3 days)
2) I see a lot of foods on both lists (best days and worst days). It would be nice if Cara noticed this and (as an option) would not display a food if it appears on both lists.

I recently wanted to start tracking my symptoms, since I have IBS and migraines, and then I stumbled upon this app. It free, which is AWESOME! I would have paid money for it because it’s so easy and simple to track symptoms, meals, headaches, mood, medications, sleep, and essentially it is everything I wanted in an app. There are NO ads which is incredible and it helps me figure out and link different foods to my symptoms and headaches, which is exactly what I wanted. The only drawback is that I wish there was one more tap where you could rate your symptoms for the day. The app automatically deduces either easy, mild, moderate, etc symptoms, but I feel like sometimes I have a different perception of yesterday I had worse symptoms than today. Overall it is incredible and super happy I downloaded it.

reviews.t: If you need help tracking symptoms from a chronic illness, look no further!
reviews.b: Cara is my #1 recommendation to any friends or family that need help tracking symptoms due to a chronic illness. You can track anything from what you eat, your bowel movements, stomach pain to headaches and menstruation. For a little over 3 years now I have been extremely ill. Sicker than I’ve ever been in my life. I’m 26, but I feel like I’m 80. In 2016, I began anemic, B-12 deficient, gained more than 50 lbs rapidly, along with an increase in symptoms from an already present GI condition. I’ve been to 2 gastroenterologists, a hematologist, rheumatologist, gynecologist, etc. and we are still unsure what is completely causing my body to remain ill. This app has been a GOD SEND for me because it tracks the number of BMs I have each day, how I feeling physically and mentally, along with what I’m eating and the medications I’m taking. Cara also makes mini graphs so I can see how things are changing week to week and month to month. I recommend this app 110%. - Rachel E.

Cara is so easy to use and so helpful! 

I’d love if it had a scanner for food items so that I didn’t have to type out ingredients, and if there were options to include portion sizes. 

It would also be amazing if it could track how long it takes to feel sick/etc. after eating certain foods. 

Overall a great app!

reviews.t: Best free BM and Food diary
reviews.b:
As someone who has had to track food and BMs since I was a kid, this app has proved to be super convenient! My favorite thing about it is that it doesn’t ask for amounts of foods that your eating, because calorie counting is not something I need to start doing again.

I love that it can connect to the health app on my iPhone so steps can be counted in the in-app data, and I love that you can track mood and stress. Plus the goal oriented layout keeps me motivated to continue logging!

I’ve talked to my therapist about this app and she said she wants to start recommending it to all of her clients!

Been using daily for ~3 weeks and am loving the app so far. Super easy to use interface and has nice customizations to what you’d like to track. As an analytics driven person it would be nice to have some more detailed analysis in the app, but the data can be exported as a csv which is great. Definitely would recommend
Great app and customer support!

reviews.t: So much better than a notepad
reviews.b: So glad I found this app. Easy to use and great options on what to track. My only feedback is I wish you could add other drinks besides water in a separate section.
I'm just getting started and it seems pretty good but does it really not offer the option to track energy levels as a symptom? That seems like a pretty major oversight

Cara is a really neat app if you’re looking for a food and symptom tracker! It gives you the foods you ate on your best three days and your worst three days, which is pretty neat as well. It’s also good to track stress levels, hours of sleep, headaches, workouts, and water intake. A lot of that stuff requires manual input, but it’s nice to look back on the day and see I didn’t drink a lot of water, which might be why I have a headache in the evening. 

Regarding suggestions: I’d love to see some more in-depth and interactive graphs/data/feedback with all the data we input. There is a way to correlate data, but the graph output is super basic. More information on foods that consistently cause issues and foods that don’t as opposed to only three days would be helpful - like data over time...for example 90% of days you drank milk, you also reported an upset stomach. Just a thought! Being able to alphabetize favorite meals would be nice, too!

Overall, this is a great app! Just hoping to be able to use the data more than what the app currently allows.
So easy to use and enter info.
It would be great if you could choose more than “food from the previous day” since it can be more or less for some.

I’m about 3 days into using this app, but I am probably going to delete it. Overall, it’s easy to use and intuitive, and I’m starting to see some correlations of interest although it hasn’t yet begun to report all of the information it apparently will after a few more days, like best and worst food days. 

That said, it does some weird things that I either dislike or despise. 

The worst so far is that yesterday, it reported to my diet app (LoseIt!) that I had exercised for an hour and burned 400 calories doing so. Unfortunately, I didn’t do a darn thing but go about my usual, almost completely sedentary day. In fact, during the specific hour reported, I had just stumbled out of bed and was in the bathroom! I’ve also been sick enough lately that there is *no way* I could even *possibly* exercise for anywhere near that long!

There is also *nowhere* in Cara I might have reported such a thing, nor that I can tell that is pulling info from my Apple Watch, and I can find nowhere that there are even settings for exercise other than the Workout section where one has to *manually* input exercise as with all other data. It also reported this exercise “bonus” to the watch activity center, so now *those* stats are all screwed up! 

When recording water drunk, it only allows you to choose number of glasses, not the actual amount drunk. I have been using Water Minder to track my overall liquid intake, and Cara does report to that as 8oz per glass. I have to edit it for the correct amount, though - and still have to manually add the other types of liquid, like soup and juice, some of which WM discounts in volume to account for the lower percentage of actual water in the beverage, which helps me keep my overall intake correct. I’m not sure, but I think they may *both* be reporting water to LoseIt! because that is tending to show much more water drunk than I have actually taken in. This is completely not cool. 

I am completely committed to these two apps, so Cara seems to be just screwing up their data, along with that of the Activity Center. 

Finally, and most importantly for an app intended for tracking gut activity, which is why I got it, it does not allow for any indication of the size and volume of bowel movements. One tiny little bit or a mountain of sludge, all it allows for reporting is what it looks like in texture and consistency. If you want to track color, you have to do that with added tags, which I suppose one could use for amount, too, but that would be far less useful than a visual numeric or “a little, average, a lot” kind of scale that could be seen visually in the charts. 

I think I had to actually pay for this one, didn’t I? If so, I want my money back because of the nonconsensual and wildly inaccurate data it is somehow coming up with and sending everywhere unbidden.

reviews.t: Answer to my problems and probably yours too!
reviews.b:
Cara is awesome. It makes tracking my bowel movements sooo much easier. I highly recommend it as a valuable tool for everyone. It is particularly useful for people with IBS, but I could see the value of it for any number of reasons: heartburn, celiac’s, intolerances, and more. Even if you are some sort of super human with none of those things, it is great for just generally knowing your body better- what to feed it, what not to, what makes it rebel and despise you, what makes it more energized and happy, etc. 

NOTE: I honestly don’t log my food often on the app. I mainly log my bowel movements. So I can’t attest to other negative reviews regarding the accuracy of good vs bad days triggers. I will say that it is a bit cumbersome to log food, and I would be happy to see that updated. Regardless, the app still retains its value in providing a simple method to track your poops. 

My personal story and why I love it:

I have irritable bowel syndrome, but it took a long time for me to get diagnosed. Part of the reason for this was that when I went to the doctor and was asked to describe my poop, what it looks like and how often it happens, my response was always something really eloquent and useful like, “uhhhhhhhh I don’t know. Abnormal sometimes? Generally not everyday? My poop is poop-like.”  And no I couldn’t expand on that or give a frequency estimate. I couldn’t tell them what foods or drinks may have caused my vague complaints of abnormalities. 

I only have so much brain space, and I don’t want to fill that space with what my poop patterns are like. I don’t want to take the time and brain space to memorize that! Seriously, is anyone actually able to answer that question off the top of their head? Who stores that sort of information? Well, my brain automatically sends that data right to spam. 

Eventually, I started writing down notes about my bowel movements. This was better but still problematic. I wasn’t sure what details were worth noting, and I found that when I gave doctors pages and pages of handwritten poop notes in response to their questions, they did two things. 1) They looked at me like I was a weirdo. And, 2)They looked at the notes like I was asking them to hand wash dishes. They’d fruitlessly glance at my notes, but no one would actually spend time reading them. Although, I can’t say I blame them; it’s not like I’m handing them a fascinating novel. 

Then I found this app and it was the answer to all my problems! I still have IBS of course, but the app makes actually explaining it and managing it so much easier!!  

The app gives a basic outline of notable things to track, and allows you the flexibility to add your own tags for things you find significant enough to track. It uses the data and entries you put in to provide nifty charts and percentages that help outline what your poops are like and what foods/drinks can trigger the bad poops. Cara is the solution to the dreaded mystifying doctor question, “what are your poops like?”

This app is so easy! If a food isn’t there, you just create it with no hassle. It just doesn’t get any easier to track what you are putting in your mouth. You can create your own symptoms and basically personalize all of it EASILY WITH NO EXTRA ANNOYING STEPS!  I totally love that. I haven’t even gotten into all of the features, but if the most important thing for you right now is to track what you ingest and symptoms of all kinds, then you have got to get this. I can’t believe this is free because it’s really wonderful.

I’m a newly diagnosed diabetic, and have been searching for a free ‘food journal’ to help manage my blood sugar. It took a bit of trial and error but I think I’ve found the perfect app! 

It has so many bells and whistles that I can’t believe this is available for free! Many thanks to the developers of this app! You are helping to save many lives out there 😃

reviews.t: Works great but want one more feature
reviews.b: I love the way this is set up and functions. But please add peeing as something to track. I haven’t found another app that tracks as well as this one. It’s a bodily function of equal importance! Thanks for a great product.
And you will be perfect

I’ve been struggling with food control issues and chronic stomach pain for ten years. At the very least Cara is helping me be more mindful of my intake. I’m hopeful it will help me crack the code. But I’d like it to include a meditation tracker. Please add!
Promising but need a lot more work.
This app is amazing for anyone who Wants to track their diet and health
I’m trying to make an account, and it says 12 and up, but it only lets you put in the age 16 and up.

reviews.t: Really good and versatile, expect improvements with proliferation
reviews.b: I really like Cara. I had previously been trying to track lots of things via a sort of diary app. Cara makes this much more organized (I’m not inherently organized). I expect Cara to get better and better with more wide use. I can’t say for sure how to make it better but I’ll bet the developers do, going on how well the structure is now. Definitely worth a try!
Great app but it now crashes ever since I enabled passcode. Cannot even open app to disable.

This is a great app, so helpful. It’s what I needed to figure out what’s making me sick and what not to eat and what I could eat. 

Could you please fix the Wheat Bread button on the app because when I click it it says I had white bread for breakfast. If I at white bread I would be sick daily. My dr would ask why???!!!!
Easy to log data and see patterns.
Worthless app that doesn't share/send the data you input into it.
Super helpful in recording everything I do.

reviews.t: It’s good as far as I’m concerned.
reviews.b: I like the different things to track, but I am still in my 1st and 2nd week, so I might update my rating then

This app being free and also ad-free is almost unbelievable. It’s a great tool to track basically anything food related and the export/desktop browser view is just fantastic. Big shout out to the dev team behind this masterpiece!

reviews.t: Excellent app to help track my symptoms, only one suggestion
reviews.b: This app is a great app.  Has all the categories required to help analyze your specific problem.  The only category that I suggest they add and track is your blood pressure.  I track my bp on my own and notice that when my pain is high, so is my blood pressure and when my pain is low, so is my bp. I have to add this data in my notes.  Would like to see it link to my OMRON bp app or my health app.
I usually don’t rate apps but this is a pretty good app. Definitely helps me track what is causing my pain. It can be as simple and as complex as you would like.

Concept is what I am looking for although navigating the app is far from intuitive.  I’d like to be able to see my menstrual cycle phase is my dashboard and also my water consumption.  Overall, the app is serving its purpose, with room for improvement.

I have been using it for a couple days & so far I like it. The only thing I don’t like is how mood doesn’t seem to have as much impact on symptom score as the other categories. I use it for my depression/anxiety. I may be having a horrible day, but it still says my symptom score is mild.

reviews.t: Good app but needs more functionality
reviews.b: This app is generally good for its purpose, but there are a few simple features it lacks that can make it annoying to use. When you save favorite meals, it would be great if there were a way to reorder them, whether alphabetically or in a custom fashion, to make things easier to find. It would also be great to be able to search favorite meals. When you have many entered, it can be hard to find what you are looking for. Finally, it would be great if you could enter multiple favorite meals in the same entry, rather than having to save and choose another item to enter each time.

Today I opened the app to find it claiming that Curry and Lactose are ingredients from my best days. Only, I specifically entered those ingredients on my worst days. I am clinically diagnosed with Lactose intolerance and it makes me sick every time. I also just spent a whole weekend with diarrhea following a curry. I entered both of those ingredients into Cara to remind myself never to eat them again.

Yet, somehow it’s “tracking” decided those two ingredients were “best days.” Perhaps it thinks 12 watery bowel movements in a day is good? I tried switching settings to register the previous day and then back to the “day of.” This seemed to make no difference. I have been tracking all foods, bowel movements, and stomach pain for an entire month. I was extremely disappointed to see how poorly it is interpreting the data I entered. I think I’ll have to go back to tracking on my own with a good journal. Very disappointed in how unreliable the dashboard results of this app are.

Good app and makes it easy to log. The only thing I would like this app to improve on is the ease of comparing food and symptoms within a particular day to help isolate for example, how breakfast vs lunch may have caused symptoms.

There are no ads in this free app, and if it weren’t free I would gladly pay for it. I have IBS and GERD, and tracking all of my symptoms can be difficult. I usually use MyFitnessPal for food intake but because I don’t have premium, I can’t see the times I ate so I couldn’t correlate foods with symptoms. But this app, Cara, tracks the minute you enter something. You can retroactively add something as well, but only in 15-minute increments. My phone is basically always on me anyway so that’s not a bother. My only complaint is that it doesn’t count “today” as “today” until after 4 am. Sometimes my symptoms cause me to wake at 3 in the morning and it will track it as if it’s the day before. Honestly this would’ve been perfect when I worked swing shift.... oh well. 
I like that you can add your own meds, foods, create favorite meals so if you eat the same food every day you just select it. No worries about calorie/nutrient info either like in MFP, so you just type what you ate and add it. You can add your own tags in the symptoms, plus there is a journal tab too so you can take notes in the same entry as your food/symptoms. Really, can’t ask for better. This is an ideal app for any symptoms for any ailment.

I have been using this for a while and for those who are having crashing issues... I suggest updating your iOS. I haven’t had a single functioning issue with this app yet.

reviews.t: App started crashing every time I open it
reviews.b: I was really enjoying this until it started crashing immediately every time I open it. This has been going on for close to a week, and I’ve tried doing a hard restart of the app and restarting my phone.

I love the idea of this app and how simple and easy it is to use multiply times a day. However, i find that the analysis provided isn’t digestible to me. No pun intended. As the end user, i don’t connect with the results. More so- I don’t understand what it means or how to interpret the app so i Can make better choices. I think it would be nice to have a daily rating that pops up with a happy face for good, sad face for bad etc like a really short , concise daily message blatantly stating how my day was and what I can do better.

Good potential but I want to use this app to figure out what is contributing to my babies eczema but it seems that even though the app allows you to record many different categories of things it only uses a few of them to calculate the good and bad days.  I think it would be nice if the app allowed you to choose the categories that you want analyzed and then perhaps had you give a rating to that category for the day. (Such as 1-5 on the condition of your skin...or even a better than, worse than, same as the day before or something.  It would also be great if the app noticed a correlation of foods from the day of to two days before as I know that the effects of the foods can be some time after eating them...particularly with breastfed babies.  Also, I definitely like the idea of a barcode reader for those convince foods with long ingredients lists.

I have tried contacting support almost 5 times now about how when I try to open the app, it automatically closes and does this like 10 times until it finally opens. How am I supposed to use an app that won't open or takes several tries to do so? Please fix this as I do like this app's purpose.

I have some requests for the developers!  1) The ability to take a photo of an ingredient list (like a Oreos or something) and have cara populate them into the food part of the app. Example: adding tomato sauce triggered fructose as a bad ingredient within the sauce but the tomato sauce I picked didn’t have any additives, only real whole ingredients 2) allow certain categories to be hidden once filled out for that day ie: exercise or sleep 3) allow the ability to hide some of the prepopulated symptoms so the list isn’t as long ie: skin symptoms has a super long list 4) ability to select a specific date range to view trend or historic data 5) also allow the user to identify which ingredients are considered bad ie: known food allergies, food additives (guar gum), preservatives
This app tracks everything! And with the ability to correlate I can finally make sense of everything I need to track. Thank you Cara!!!

reviews.t: Great for tracking and correlating multiple symptoms with foods and stress factors
reviews.b:
I’ve struggled with stomach issues and headaches for years and this is the first app that has really acted as that food, mood and symptoms journal my doctor asks you to keep.

It’s been to see how certain foods or stress correlate to stomach, body, etc symptoms.

So far I'm liking the app to track my food, sleep, etc. BUT it would also be nice to be able to scan a barcode for your food as well as just put in ingredients. I like the scanner feature for supplements.

I thought this app looked promising, and it probably is, but it certainly is not intuitive. I see no way to track symptoms. At first I thought I needed to track food for six days and then I could start tracking symptoms but after tracking food for several days it still says six more days six more days six more days. So I see no utility.  I read the FAQs I’ve tapped on every active button in the app and just am not able to make it work. Proceed with caution in terms of time investment. Clearly it must be working for some people who are less tech savvy than I am but this is my experience. I’ve heard Monash Uni has an app that helps with the FODMAP scale which I may try next.

Overall a really great app.  The tracking aspects are much better than other apps I’ve used. I wish the best/worst foods worked a little better though.

Pros: 
Tracking of multiple symptoms 
Place to make notes for additional symptoms such as allergies 
Can export your data
Can setup reminders

Cons
The best and worst foods seem to be based on calendar days rather than foods you ate within the past 24 hours.  For example, if I have symptoms in the morning from something I ate for dinner yesterday it doesn’t seem to connect those.

reviews.t: awesome app, could be more detailed
reviews.b: I love this app for monitoring my chronic illnesses. It’s great that you can add tags to entries, but I wish you could filter the correlation graphs by tags or that Cara generated correlation stats based on tags (headache vs headache with a migraine tag, for example). I also wish you could add specific qualifiers (like “this is an ingredient with dairy” to custom ingredients you add to Cara). I also wish you could add custom entry types (like “allergic reaction” for me) and customize sliders and existing tags. Overall, Cara is by far the best app for this that I’ve found, but it could be more sophisticated.

This app has a bit of learning curve, but it does what it does very well. The one change I'd like to see is the ability to add user specified trackers. There are several other things I have to track, (medications, symptoms for non-bowel issues) that I have to track, and having to switch back and forth with other trackers is a HUGE PITA, but the Notes section just isn't enough. That, and the fact that there seems to be no easy way to contact developers to make a suggestion, are the only things that dinged a star off. It would also be nice to have the ability to tell the app to disregard sick days in figuring bad days, as I keep being told that my worst days were ones I was sick (I know that!) and the foods I eat when I'm sick are assumed to be the cause. They aren't. But it's a solid app overall, and I'm still using it.

reviews.t: Red Bull is not just a soda
reviews.b:
Frustrating. Good UI, but bad data model.

When you eat it wants you to name the meal, but it’s just a text entry with no auto complete. Everything is Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, or Snack, why you gotta make me type?

Then I tried to record a Red Bull. No matter what I do it wants to store that as “carbonated soda”. That’s wrong. It’s not just a soda and I want to track those separately. 

As if that wasn’t bad enough I can’t figure how they fund the app. That makes me think they want to harvest my data.

reviews.t: Was just what I was looking for. AMAZING!
reviews.b: I love cara. It has everything I need to track my food, stool, stress, and digestive pains to ensure you that they will help. For me, I have stomach pains all the time and cara is giving me suggestions about food categories I should take out of my diet and it’s really helping me. I totally recommend cara and think it’s a great app if that’s what your looking for!

reviews.t: Why wont they show results for beef?
reviews.b: Ive had several meals which shared multiple meat products and for some reason on the “best three days section” one meat such as chicken or lamb will show up, but beef will not. Even if the beef was a part of the same meal. I ate a sausage made of ostrich and beef. I listed both on the list of ingredients, but I only see data for the ostrich. I looked around for an issue in the settings option but found nothing. Its important to leave bias out of scientific studies. Its unfortunate that an app that shapes peoples health through diet is behaving that way.

The app covers a LOT of info (food water meds mood etc) but doesn’t go into enough depth.  Also, I feel like I have to click a lot to make one entry. The process of recording your food could definitely be easier, like have a suggestion lists of the individual users top breakfast food when it’s around the time they eat breakfast maybe? It’d be awesome if your personal top IMAGES of food was presented when you open the food option, rather than having to type. Also, it says “Meal” and then “Ingredients” when it should say “Meal” then “Dishes” and then “ingredients” for each dish. Also, QUANTITY! One egg or one cookie etc is very different from three when acting as a factor for health. So a quantity option would be very helpful in accuracy. Lastly, the “three best days” didn’t seem to take in account meds, which, for many people, highly effects what days would be the best or worst. I am keeping this app until I find a more thorough one, but hopefully this one is updated :) I’d definitely pay for the app if it was more thorough, but at this stage, I’m glad it’s free.
AND it syncs to Apple health kit

This is a great app for tracking everything that goes in and goes out. However, the food/symptom relation is practically useless. It only tracks symptoms based on the food from that day or the day before... so unless you eat the same thing all day one day and only have digestion issues the same day is it helpful. I don’t know why it doesn’t track based on typical digestion times. If that was the case this app would be fantastic. Works great otherwise.

reviews.t: Has Potential But Date Input Not Working
reviews.b: I have tried repeatedly to correct the dates and times on entries that are incorrect but when I select “save,” nothing happens. The entry error also happens automatically. For example I just made a new entry at 00:31 “TODAY” (Saturday early morning of 23rd) but the entry keeps the date Friday 22nd when I try to correct it. Needless to say, I can’t track anything if the entries are stuck on the wrong days and times. Hope they fix this or let me know what is going wrong.

Please make this app available on the Apple Watch!

Additionally, a way to organize an active  medication list with medicine reminders would be fantastic.

reviews.t: I like What it’s meant to do
reviews.b: Cara has a lot of info and the ability to track many issues. But when I got it - it was not intuitive. It needs a tutorial run through that can be turned on or off.  Also I’m not 100% sure how it correlates food to health/mood but I think it should correlate for 24hours after you eat because many foods make me sick the next day. But I’ll feel ok on the day I eat them.
Really focused and simple.  Way to go

reviews.t: Really great for trying to analyze food allergies.
reviews.b: I have EoE and am on a 60 day elimination diet, and Cara is helping me do the hard work of trying to isolate food allergens.

The food entry interface is just as confusing as the previous symptom tracker I just gave up on. I made an error and it wasn’t obvious how to delete an entry from my favorites list. Also when I tried to choose and ingredient to give its own ingredients I couldn’t do it. It should be more obvious and flexible. I would like to edit my favorites list without having to be making an entry at all. If I could just flexibly create my favorites list myself I would like this app a lot. As it is its too frustrating and not created for older folks who are not all fine with a lot more awkwardness in their apps.

I have been using this app daily for just over  a month. I was diagnosed with Celiac Disease about two months ago and was looking for a way to track my food intake and any symptoms I was experiencing. 
So far I am very please with Cara. It is very user friendly. It took no time at all to learn all the ins and outs. I felt very confident using the app after just a few days. 
This is very basic in so far as it does not track calories or nutrients, but you can add the basic ingredients to your meals and even save meals you eat frequently to make input easier. This is helpful for me to see if any certain foods or ingredients are causing any digestive issues. 
You are also able to track those digestive issues, along with water intake, workout, period, vitamin or medication intake, mood and stress, to see how you’re feeling correlates to the food you’ve eaten. 
One area that I would love to see improvement is perhaps being able to sort through the saved meals to make them easier to find when I am looking for something I know I have already saved. Currently the app saves those meals in the order they were entered which takes time to scroll through all of my entries. I like that I can go back and edit those entries but it did take me a while to realize how to change the name of my saved meals; it isn’t an obvious field but you can hold your finger over the text and place your cursor in the name to make changes...originally I thought that was a static field until I just tried to put my cursor in it and it worked.  
Also, it would be nice if down the line the app linked in some way to the data on manufactured foods so that I could search for the food I am entering and it automatically populates the ingredients.
I also like that I can add fields to the tracking for my workout, mood, and pain levels. By doing so I am using the app to track other occurrences of non-celiac related issues to keep a record of when I was experiencing, let’s say back pain or skin related problems, or even how far I ran in my daily workout. 
Overall I think this app is great if you are looking for a straight forward way to keep track of your diet for the purpose of digestive problems. If you are looking to track your calories or nutrients then this won’t suffice. Even the improvement areas I mentioned above aren’t really anything negative about the app, they’re just my “wishlist” things if I wanted to build the perfect app for my personal needs. On a non-personal level I think this app works really well.

reviews.t: Amazing!!! Thank you for offering this amazing app.
reviews.b:
First review of an app I’ve ever left, been on iOS for years lol. I just had to share, this is exactly what I needed to send to my gastroenterologist. This is a well polished app and even for fear of it changing because I couldn’t pay monthly fees, I’m amazed this service is free with the web portal and extra services. 

You guys are truly doing something that has an impact on peoples lives and just wanted to say thank you!

reviews.t: Best app to see about food and stress sensitivity
reviews.b: I use this app to see if any foods are effecting my fibromyalgia and it works great. The only thing I wish they would add is: In the monthly breakdown where you can correlate, I wish it could correlate symptoms with certain food groups like “lactose” “glisten” etc so I can see how my pain and symptoms change depending on the frequency I’m eating those foods.

I love this app. I’ve used it everyday for 305 consecutive days. I track everything I can, and stick to it daily. I love using this app but I think it could use some updates. I love how much the app includes and will continue to use it but I do wish there were more/updated features. I do like that when there isn’t an option for something that it allows you to free text it in as an option (under most every section). Overall, very great app
“Food on my best 3 days” does not work.
It’s so AMAZING and easy to use. It really helps track and make sure your healthy and to let your doctor know (if wanted) how you are doing. So far I’m loving Cara!!

This app has a great concept and I was really looking forward to it, but in the few times I attempted to use it, I was automatically booted out of the app. The app will only work when I delete it from my phone and then re-download it. After I use it a few times, I am forced out of the app again. I’m not sure what is causing this issue but I have not experienced this problem with any other app.
Thank you!

This app has really helped to track my symptoms to determine what they are and how often they happen. It is nice that This allows you to track your pain throughout the day as some apps only allow a once a day measurement. I also have liked all the graphs to compare the symptoms to determine patterns. The final thing I have liked is the ability to add your own descriptions to the preset categories to track the things that are most relevant to me. I would highly rate this app to someone who is looking to identify patterns in their symptoms.
Great app. Easy to use once you figure it out. Wish you were not locked into the bumps on the stool. Sometimes I’m in between.

reviews.t: Very nice and pleasant to track things ...
reviews.b:
There are some things I would like to be able to track more easily, but overall it's the best and easiest general tracker I've found ... I'm using it to record meals, mental state, and just general thoughts and notes throughout the day, as well as poop! Haha.
You had me at "poop tracker!" 😁 Lol.
I think it's maybe intended for IBD, but even though I don't have IBD, I'm finding it helpful. It would be even more helpful if it could track more consortia and things, etc, but it's still quite nice. I was

this app is exactly what i was looking for to help me narrow down what my body does and doesn't like. my only complaint is that when i enter something for let's say 3am one day, it automatically moves it to the previous day's overview. i understand that's considered late to most people, but i go into work at 4am some days so having my breakfast disappear to the previous day is pretty annoying.

This app seemed very promising. But after entering a bunch of data today I’m now locked out and there’s no US customer service from the website. I enabled a security code and Touch ID on my iPhone XS. Now when the app launches it immediately crashes (I see the PIN screen for a flash). I suspect it broke because the XS has Face ID instead of Touch ID. But in any case now I’m locked out and can’t fix it. 

I also couldn’t figure out how to have Cara see my steps from the Apple Health app. It was enabled to share that data, but I wasn’t seeing that info in Cara as workouts.
I'm switching from an iPhone 6 to an XR at the moment... The app works fine on the 6 but on the XR, when it gets to the point when I'm supposed to enter my code, it crashes. 😕

reviews.t: Quick response time! Old -> Can’t get data and no response from the team
reviews.b:
They responded quickly and fixed my issue. There are minor caveats I would say but I really like what the team is doing. I know some physios who are very interested in this as a logging solution! 

Old response
——

The app is simple and useful. It’s definitely easy to use and stick with. The analysis is a little simplistic though so I requested my data as a csv through the button in the menus. I’m getting a server error and when I message support I received no response for basically a whole day. The chat says “usually replies within minutes”, so it would seem like they are bad at analysis of their chat response times... 

Anyway if I actually get access to this, I would give a 5 star rating in a heartbeat.

reviews.t: Great UI - restrictive in data input
reviews.b:
I really wanted to love this app with all my heart. I was taking pictures, being really on top of things but sometimes, inputting things felt a bit manual by ingredient when it couldn’t find the meal.

My biggest number 1 complaint is not being able to put in the amount/serving size. This is HUGE. My dietician was like great, we know the what, but we need the how many. You could eat half a jar of peanut butter and all you would be able to put it “peanut butter”. Get what I’m saying?

If you need better search, and more granular control, use MyMacros. It’s very very data driven. It’s not as pleasing to the eye but you will really be able to track everything down to gram.

Face ID crashes the app. Wish the food tracking was integrated with some sort of food database to make entries easier. Aside from that, this is a solid, useful app to track your health and help identify issues!

To get an export all your data is sent to Cara and then emailed to you. This means Cara gets all your data and it’s passed through email which is not a secure medium. Please don’t take my data. Give me an option to export without having to use your servers and for all data to stay on my device.

The app is useless. When I add tracking data at a specific time and then bowel movements half an hour later, the app does not update my “best/worst foods” list. For example, if I add that I ate rice at 6 o’clock and that I felt bloated and had stomach pain half an hour later, Cara does not update to this entry. I have no idea how their tracking works and it makes absolutely no sense.

reviews.t: App was great but update today lost all info
reviews.b: Totally lost all my tracking info after today’s update. App tells me I can restore, I go through the restore process... it starts to say I have a “streak” of info but then pops to “Begin Cara” and makes me go through the entire initial set up... and my info on s gone!

The first thing I noticed was that there is no barcode scanning. I would gladly pay for this app if that feature were introduced.

Another category/tab that I’d like to see is weather (humidity, barometric pressure, sunrise/set pollen counts, heck... even moon phases). I’m sure those environmental things have an effect on appetite and physical wellbeing. For now I will be adding any random stuff like this into the notes.

Really looking forward to see if this app can help me to pinpoint what is going with my bod since all labs and tests (thankfully) show no areas of concern. It’s incredibly frustrating to deal with constant pain and discomfort with no explanation.

5th star will be earned when barcode scanning is added (and works). :)

Did I mention barcode scanning?

reviews.t: Exactly what I’ve been looking for!
reviews.b: I have been dealing with migraines and digestion problems for years now, and my doctor told me that I needed to start tracking almost everything because there were too many possible factors. Now I can keep an eye on all of it and hopefully get down to the bottom of this! I love that it tracks so many things, including your food & water intake, stomach issues, digestion, headaches, general pains, mood, stress level, monthly cycle, skin, sleep, workouts, medications, etc. Most helpful health app I’ve found!

I was also looking for a replacement for tracking food in my bullet journal, while I love bullet journaling I like having this app on my phone to help me start better tracking my food/symptoms

One critique, I wish their database of known vitamins and foods were a bit larger. However, if a vitamin, supplement or food doesn't exist it is easy enough to add yourself. 

I'm looking forward to taking my notes tracked in Cara to a specialist - instead of being at a loss for words when I show up to the appointment.
This app is a great way of recording everything from food and exercise to stress levels and emotional well-being.

I love this app. You can leave your feelings, stomach problems, what you ate. Even if you don’t have IDS, you can so use this app. One thing I love, is that they give you an over all level to your day. It gives you a better idea of if you’re worrying to much over small things. I used to worry so much because I though I was so unhealthy, but now I see that’s not true. I know it’s not meant for this, but I also like to just track my food. Not even calories, just what I’m eating. It can help your doctor better understand what’s wrong, and help you make healthier decision because you know exactly what you’re eating. I love it.
Cara is a super easy way to keep track of your meals and monitor any symptoms that go along with the food you eat. I’m really excited about this app!

This app has helped my track my digestion and all the factors that could be contributing to it. I love that you can send the report to your doctor and it tracks your best and worst days along with what you were doing on those days. Very easy to use and quick to record.

reviews.t: Helped me pinpoint what was causing pain.
reviews.b: Cara is very useful for any GI distress and getting to the bottom of it. In today’s day and age, with healthcare being what it is, cara helps you take your health into your own hands.
Very useful for tracking IBS symptoms and possible causes. Has a nice graphic for seeing correlations and trends.
I have a chronic illness. This app makes it so easy and helps me track ALL my symptoms so that I can later go to my dr and just say “here look this is what I’ve been going through” help me.

This app is amazing. It is exactly what I need to keep track of everything in one place, either just to see the trends of how I’m feeling compared to certain foods I’ve eaten, or my sleep patterns and it has helped when seeing my doctor. It has it all!

My only caveat is that I wish it would read all categories from Apple Health as well as write them, as I use other tracking apps and would prefer to only enter data once. reviews.b:
The app is good but it is all or nothing one one device.  I transferred to my iPad which is only wireless and then when I tried to move back to phone it failed.

I need something that I can use across all my devices at the same time.

I’ve been trying to pinpoint the cause of stomach pains. This app is a great diary for any issues you are having with your body...even if you are completely healthy and just want to keep track of what’s “normal” for you...I use it everyday and I can send the info to a DR with no issues. No matter what you’re looking to track this app is incredible. Meds, food, mood, even exercise and periods. If you’re looking for a way to record your daily life and then be able to look back over the data you’re in the right place. Love it!!!

It’s VERY easy to use ; I like that it offers a place to add a descriptions and has a notes page . Really like it so far . If I choose I can sync with Apple health and email to myself and docs . After using for a week, with 3 days having no BM, the tracker is very faulty. The tracker allows a entry for none. BUT it counts in the average and other stats as if I had a BM. That is pointless!! WTH. I tried getting ahold of support and no response. I am very frustrated.

reviews.b: It’s handy to log food intake in the moment, but I need to be able to print daily logs directly from the app to hand over to my doctor. It only offers to send the data to my email address and after an hour of waiting for it to pop up in my email, I still haven’t received anything. I’ve tried multiple times. It’s SEVERELY inconvenient so I will have to find a different app. Without the ability to print the data, this app is useless for me.
