reviews.b: I’d give this app twelve stars if they had stronger tools for analyzing correlations (I.e. not just relying on the fact that graphs “look the same”) AND if you could analyze the correlations between symptoms and a set of foods (like all foods containing eggs or a set of foods of your choosing).
You have to agree to their Privacy policy before you can use it, but you can’t read the policy because it’s hidden behind the keypad, so you have to accept it by default. No thanks.

I have had stomach problems for over a year. I wish I would have found this app sooner. I think it’s amazing you can export reports to your provider - this will greatly help my internist as I will most likely be headed to a GI specialist soon.

reviews.t: Amazing concept and implementation, iffy on some details
reviews.b:
Overall I do really like the app. It looks nice and is fairly straightforward, and I appreciate that there are so many different things you can track and log while getting to pick and choose which of those things you yourself want to focus on. For the spirit behind the app and the execution, it's five stars.

However, there are a few glaring problems that make the app less than ideal to actually use, and thus knock off a couple of those stars.

First of all, I wish there was a settings option for toggling like... the country of origin of the suggested food/ingredients. Because I can tell there's clearly British or possibly European developers behind this app, and it leads to some weird ingredient suggestions when I try to enter in something. For example, an attempt to add sweet tea led to the suggestion of "soft drinks", but in the US soft drinks are carbonated beverages, and sweet tea is just brewed tea with sugar served cold, and would never in a million years be a soft drink; popping up "iced tea" and "sugar (white)" would make more sense. Frozen custard also kept turning up "pudding" and nothing else--but here, custard is a richer version of ice cream. 

And a lot of stuff is just plain missing, which I understand not having everything in the world (powdered sugar, for example), but some omissions just seem odd (cupcakes???) and I figure is missing more due to cultural differences than the developers limiting the food that's included. So I'd like an option to toggle to something else other than the British/European foods and ingredients.

I realize I can change ingredients myself, and I do, but it adds in extra steps and wastes time that could be solved by having a few different regional "menus" to choose from where the ingredients better reflect the food you personally eat.

It's also really bizarre and frustrating that if you enter in a mood you had or pain you felt at 1am, 3am, whatever, it's put on the PREVIOUS day. From what I can tell it starts counting stuff as the new day at around 4 in the morning rather than midnight, and that's just strange. If people want to count stuff that happened to them in the early hours of the day as the previous day I mean more power to them, but I'd really like the option to be able to control that. It throws me off when I'm trying to refer back to something at 1:30 and it's like "oh, right, they put it on the previous day... for some reason." Like please... put in a setting to change that.

I also feel like you should be able to select multiple types of stool at once rather than just the single option along the slider. Because sometimes your body isn't feeling that consistent, and you might be experiencing a lot of things at once. I don't want to go into too much detail here, but why a slider for One Type of something at all, when all the other selections let you reflect that a lot of things might be happening at the same time?

If you want to keep track of your food, drink, sleep, poop, mental state, etc., I am not sure you will find a better app. As lots of other people state in the comments, this is an indispensable tool for people with IBS and other digestive issues.

However, I do have a few criticisms:

[EDIT ADDED: For both the “Food on my best/worst days” sections of the main home screen, I found a toggle switch located in the settings (little wheel/cog icon) that allows the user to set “Food from the previous day” as causative of the symptoms - this eliminates criticism #1 below, but I leave it here in case any reader had the same concern.]

1) The app reports back what you ate on your worst and best days - this is brilliant in theory and a computer (your phone) can surely sort through this complexity much better than you could using paper and pen. However, telling me what I ate on the literal worst days doesn’t really capture what actually caused the problem. It’s really what I ate the 12-24hrs BEFORE the episode started that counts. If the food that made you sick took place in real time, well, who couldn’t keep track of that? All of this presumably gets more accurate over time as you enter more data (I’m almost 2 week’s in), but it still tells me that food I ate on a bad day, after the worst of the episode is already over, correlates with the bad day. This definitely needs a programming tweak.

2) It would be very nice if you could Apple Share meal entries with your spouse, partner, friend, etc. who might be along for the ride. When I have already entered the info., why can’t I just send it directly to my wife and save her the hassle?

3) Naming conventions can be tricky and cause issues - for example, if you use the in-app term “Beef” one day and “burger” the next, the app doesn’t see those as the same group (so far as I can tell). Same for plurals - e.g., the system uses “Blueberry” - but I have also entered “blueberries” and you can end up with weird things like each one showing up separately in foods associated with good and bad days simultaneously. The answer is to be very consistent in your naming, but this is easier said than done and the system could do better here.

Suggestion: Add another slider to Sleep that allows the user to qualitatively record not just how long, but their assessment of the sleep - and add another related output to the home screen (like with stress and symptoms).

I could come up with a few other nitpicks, but those are my major comments. Overall it’s pretty darn good and could be great with some modifications. It’s an excellent journal - the analysis needs some additional programming.
Finally able to track what foods make my symptoms better or worse. After years of doctors, this is a simple and awesome solve!

I’ve just been using this app for a few days, but I’m really impressed by how easy it is to use, the clean interface, and the level of specificity you can include for the different things you track. There are some things I would improve, but they are minor—like being able to copy meals from a previous entry or being able to make comments on your entries beyond the tags provided, though to be fair, you can add new, custom tags.  The design of the user interface is encouraging through a somewhat gamified setup, and you earn points and badges for tracking your data and using the app. The app aggregates your data to help you recognize patterns you may not notice on your own. Highly recommend!

I recently went to the G.I and she said i might have IBS. Thanks to Cara I can now track everything I need to make myself better emotionally and physically so I don’t trigger any symptoms on my ibs. Best app and is very easy to use. I recommend it 100%

I really like tracking my meals, because it helps me pinpoint what foods cause stomach issues. However I wish the camera was different. You don’t have the option to set the camera for a square photo. Or you should be able to just crop the photo to the size you want instead of the narrow picture that allows you to take.
That’s really why am getting it four stars instead of five.
Tracks food, water, exercise, mood, bowel movements and more. Love that it's highly customizable. Easy to use, too. Very well designed
Cara is easy and straight forwards to use. It tracks everything I want it to. It’s free. Very worth it! Super helpful!
I got this recently and love it! So far the only change I think would be if you could have an option to have OZ of water when logging vs glasses.

Cara it’s been a part of my progress because it’s very easy to do, to right, it has everything I need to write in my goal of good health throughout my habits. When I downloaded this application I looked into others and I discovered tha Cara is easy, reliable, easy to share, easy to print I love this app.

reviews.t: Excellent app- lots of good options
reviews.b:
I love this app as it has been very helpful so far through the logging of foods and correlating them to my IBS symptoms. I have really liked the way it is set up and the variety of factors it takes into account such as headache or other pain, medication, stool and bloating. However, it would be great to see the app calculate a little more information such as taking into account a woman’s period (I always get similar digestive symptoms the day before my period regardless of what I eat) and ILLNESS! For instance, today I only ate crackers and soup because I’ve had a high fever all day long along with digestive issues, both of which are safe foods for me. Obviously whatever infection I’m fighting off is a huge factor- I would like to be able to turn off food/symptom correlation when I am obviously sick with the flu for instance. 

Thank you for this app, I look forward to seeing the improvements made!

reviews.t: Needs to have a tab for breathing issues
reviews.b: Often people who suffer from food allergies have symptoms related to breathing such as the throat closing, coughing, etc. it would be helpful to be able to notate other than as an additional note. Otherwise I am enjoying the app so far.

I find this app to be very user friendly and attractive. Entering everything from my food and drink to my mood, BM, physical symptoms was easy. I like that it remembered items or details that I needed to enter myself. I even found the act of pausing to track to be convenient and kind of fun. But...

I don’t find the results to be helpful or informative at all. “On your best day you ate...” “On your worst day you ate...” and then merely listing five items isn’t valuable feedback to me. I want to know more about the algorithms used to help me link my intake with my symptoms.

How about “Yesterday you had a headache at 3:15 PM, there are four other days this has happened, here is a list of food and drink you had within 12 hours of this event”. To me that is info I can use.

If you just want a way to track what you eat and your symptoms so you can print off a week or month for someone else to extract meaning, this app is amazing!

I suffer from chronic hives. I have been using this app to track my food intake, medications that I am trying, and notes on number and itchiness of my hives. I love the daily overview page because it shows specifics of what I typed in without having to tap on each section.

I know it is not the purpose of the app, but it would be fabulous if there was a generic section that allowed a user to type in a number (1-100) and select a severity from a rating scale (none, mild, moderate, severe).

Cara is super helpful for tracking things like bowel movements and digestive pain and correlating them to different foods, activity levels, etc. and I really appreciate the option to set a reminder after meals so I don’t forget to log details. As someone recently diagnosed with Crohn’s disease, I find it really useful to have an easy system for keeping track of these things. I’ve only been using the app for a few weeks, but my only major complaint is that it doesn’t sync with my Fitbit app, which I use to log a lot of these stats already like water intake, food, exercise, menstrual cycle, etc.
You guys misspelled diarrhea by spelling it with an “o”. (Diarrhoea).

reviews.t: Really nice—could use some new features
reviews.b: Really enjoy the ease and style of the app. Expanding food and diet options would be great, ie vegan, GF, etc.

It’s nice being able to track not only my food and water intake as well as menstruation and any pain associated with that. I’ve learned that a lot of my acne and stomach aches have really correlated with my menstruation. Really love the app so far.

There is only thing I wish for in the app. I wish the app could pull more health data from Apple Health. For example, I want to record my eating habits in one app, have that app record it into Health, and have Cara pull that data into their app without me having to enter the same thing into two separate apps.

This app is so helpful in helping me track my health protocol and progress. I have yet to find another app like it and what I love most is I can see correlations with moods and overall health when it comes to my eating, drinking, and supplements. Thanks for making such an awesome app! Not to mention it’s “free” too!

I have been looking for the right tool for my meal tracking and reaction diary this is it. I love how simple it is which helps me stay on top of things even when I am busy. I recommend it to anyone with digestion issues.

This is an app with an easy to use interface and a multitude of features. Not only can I track everything come into and out of my body, but the app uses that data to show me trends in my diet, exercise, medications, belly pain, GI distress, and much more. This has helped me discover the foods and activities that aggravate my body and the ones that make me peaceful. I’ve never been so impressed with a lifestyle app before. This app is also crafted in a way that makes you feel empowered by its tiny positive affirmations, without being annoying. I love it.
I love it!
Honestly I’m impressed with this app. It’s as complicated or simple as you want it to be. Incredibly useful! Helps to identify triggers. Seriously, amazed. Thank you. ♥️

I never would have been able to be this precise in keeping track of all my symptoms and what I ate, when I ate, what my poop looked like and how I felt. It’s been a tremendous help already in figuring out what my body is reacting on.

reviews.t: This app is pretty much perfect
reviews.b: This app is everything you need all in one place, has all the symptoms and health functions. Food, water, exercise, sleep, headaches, pains, digestion, etc. you can customize it too. Highly recommended. And you can share data.
I only use it the food tracking function to track the food for my dietician. The app is on point. Perfect for what I need.
I have had no issues with the app. It is designed very well and is exactly what I was looking for to help me track some somatic issues I have been experiencing.
It’s super comprehensive and lets you track everything and anything that might impact how you’re feeling. Not to mention it’s free.

reviews.t: A non-pressuring delight of an app!
reviews.b: A friend recommended this app to me last week... and I have to say I love it! I have IBD, but I don’t always keep as good of track of my food or my stools as I should. Cara is a very user-friendly app that encourages tracking of things such as food, stool, pain, mental health, workouts, and even menstrual cycles without making you feel guilty for missing a day or two. You can also go back and edit your entries, which is quite helpful if you remember something after the fact. I can see myself using this app for a long time to come! :)

Cara is a clear and easy way to track symptoms and it points out foods which are correlated with good symptom days versus not good symptom days. It also allows you to keep track of exercise and emotions which may be a factor related to symptoms as well.

reviews.t: Best App to Manage Food, Mood and Symptoms
reviews.b: Best app i have found and easy to use. I can track everything and correlate it to the food I eat and what I do throughout the day. I haven’t used it long enough to give it 5 stars that’s why it’s only 4

reviews.t: Really helpful in staying accountable for my diet
reviews.b: Also great for tracking digestion. Perfect for those with food allergies and on elimination diets!! Why and how is this free? Is the data we input being sold? Very useful but confused about  their business plan

This App has been extremely helpful for tracking food and stools. I’m newly diagnosed with ulcerative colitis and it’s been very helpful in helping to communicate my symptoms to my doctor and seeing the correlations. Thank you.

I am grateful for this Tracker! I love all the components it allows you to track and that you can customize it further. However I have found it confusing or difficult to save my tracking at times. Otherwise I love this app!

reviews.t: Great App, but it could have a little improvement
reviews.b: There could be an option of registering the amount of water you drink in ml or L, since a lot of people drink water from a reusable water bottle. Also, for people who have bladder issues, there could be a specific input for that as well. But overall, it’s a great and useful app!

reviews.t: Best app for gastrointestinal issues yet!
reviews.b: I have found this app so helpful. I love how easy it is to record symptoms, food, and everything in between. Great visual charts and summaries. Easy to transfer to my doctor.
I recently started using this app and I like it. Even recommended it to family and friends.  I find it’s easy to use and all my info is in one spot.

reviews.t: Perfect for tracking symptoms and possible triggers
reviews.b: I have IBS and am starting to track my triggers to find what is causing my most uncomfortable symptoms. This app is amazing for keeping track of water, food, mood, symptoms, everything. I love it.
I am so skeptical of apps because most of junk but this app is amazing!! It’s so easy to use and I know is going to be beyond helpful in the long run of tracking everything I’m impressed.
It’s designed in a really intuitive way so it’s very easy to use, tracks everything you would possibly want to track, and if there is anything you need to add, there’s also an option to add notes.

Still new to the app so I’m still learning but I like that I can track everything. It’s hard to remember some of the things that your doctors ask but with Cara I can pull it right up or transmit it to the Dr.
so helpful in tracking how gluten has been affecting me, so I can show to my doctor as I continue the process of celiac testing.

I was recently diagnosed with GERD and Cara has been super helpful in helping me keep track of what I eat and how that affects my symptoms. I started out using a fitness tracker app as a food diary, but since I’m not tracking calories, it didn’t really fit what I needed. Cara is perfect for it and has the added benefit of helping me pay attention to other healthy habits and how they affect my well-being. It’s clean and simple to use. I highly recommend it!

So far after almost a week I can see and keep track of the things I eat in an effort to see what bothers my stomach. I hope soon I will get to the bottom of it thanks to Cara! I like how it doesn’t count my calories it’s literally a food journal with an added bonus, a symptoms section as well as a few others.
Just started this week, but I’m already liking it.

I’m brand new to this app... only 3 days in. But it is really comprehensive. I love how it tracks everything that a woman needs (I’m sure it is great for men too, but we women have some female specific stuff) to help her figure out her gut issues. So far, so good!!

I am very grateful an app like this has been created. It could be a bit more user friendly. There is no explanation what your points mean or if there is a specific goal to strive for in points. I would like to see a category added to digestive symptoms. It would be helpful to track "no appetite" and "little appetite " Updated Review: I still like this app
 I have a suggestion. I would like to see an explanation of why each food item on "food on my worst days". Such as pain, digestion, type of bowel movements etc.

reviews.t: Best food allergy symptom tracking app I’ve used
reviews.b: Simple, easy to use, and has lots of tracking features. Would recommend for others with IBS or other tummy issues.

I’ve been meaning to keep a Food diary for years and this app has made it fun and easy. I can track everything in one place and be aware of how my diet and other factors affect my symptoms. It’s life changing.

I would love it if I could sync with my fitness pal so I would have to enter good twice.  Is there a way to do this? Otherwise, I can see the great potential for connecting the dots between food, exercise and mood.

reviews.t: Amazing, but needs work on food tracking
reviews.b:
This app is great for setting reminders and allows you to easily customize tags for various things that are tracked, but I think the food tracking needs some improvement. For the most part, I have cut out gluten and dairy, but when I enter ingredients, some have come up as bad despite being the gluten-free version (like gluten-free soy sauce).

Aside from the food tracking being vague in some instances, I really like this app.

This app is simple, straightforward and motivating. It is very easy to use, inputting meals, etc is user-friendly and intuitive and the point system and trend tracking are good motivators to keep you on top of your entries. You can also set notification reminders so you don’t forget on a busy day. It’s a great app to help you look holistically at your health and how you feel so you can set yourself up for more good days and to avoid bad ones. I’m really enjoying the app so far and will continue to use it daily!

This app would be great if it was more technically and functionally user friendly.
It has a lot of great ideas and foods and such, but to log in your foods and different items you chose become a huge undertaking.

I have been using this app for 3 months. I love all the options it allows me to track. I wish that it had a better monthly overview. Maybe setup like a calendar with different colors for each category that way I could easily see and track individual categories. I have seen that it can add in my steps from the health app but I have not been able to figure that out yet. This would be a five star app for me if the monthly overview was easier to read and see different categories clearly for ex: periods.
I like the details and I’m excited to see if it can track the problem-causing foods.

Tracking calories and micronutrients and all that was very overwhelming, I found that I gave up more when using apps like that because I felt like I was never doing enough of the right thing and too much of the wrong thing. And I would also omit “bad” things I ate because I felt like a failure if I didn’t live up to the perfect diet stats set forth by those apps. I’m so happy I found Cara because it’s not judgmental at all and it’s very easy and fast to use. And I love how it complies my data and helps me see what works for me and what doesn’t (although it’s a bit off at times). A really amazing app and it’s free which makes it even more perfect.

reviews.t: Have IBS for 5 years/Cara app really understands
reviews.b: Since was tracking all of my food using Google Excel Spreadsheet because a few years I could not find a good food app.  Cara solved this problem.  Easy to use via my iPhone and the information is simple to access on my phone or laptop.
This app has a tracking category for EVERYTHING.  It is perfect for my needs.

reviews.t: I love this health tracking app!
reviews.b: This app is very well designed and makes it super easy to track what you eat and how you feel (as well as sleep, exercise, period, etc). I've been meaning to track this for a while to get my gut health under control, but I wasn't able to keep up with it until Cara. It really helps me to have the notifications that I set to what time I want to be reminded to track my breakfast, lunch and dinner. I would definitely recommend this app to anyone interested in analyzing their health.

I’ve had digestive troubles most of my life, but recently it had gotten so bad I couldn’t function. This app has helped me pinpoint the foods causing the most pain and distress. Not only do I feel better, but I can think and function better!!

I'm so glad this app exists. As someone trying to figure out their digestive illness, this app is an absolute necessity to have. I got it to journal what I eat and how I poop, but this is so much more. It tells me what I should and shouldn't eat based on my longterm journaling of daily symptoms. Certain aspects of the app could stand to improve -- most of the graphs are pretty useless, and inputting ingredients could be easier/more accurate with product label scanning or whatever -- but this app really delivers on so much, i can't bring myself to deduct stars. There are a lot of nuances in correlating, customizing, and inputting data, and the user interface is A+ intuitive, straightforward and pretty. And the best part is that you can send all your data to your doctor. Fantastic!  I can't recommend it enough for anyone trying to keep a food diary, stool diary, or track any kind of illness symptoms.

I started using Cara to help me and my doctor figure out my chronic heartburn. I've been keeping track for several months. I got used to the new interface, but it’s hard to answer basic questions for my doctor. If my doctor asks, “when did this start?” I can’t easily answer that question without tapping day by individual day and my doctor doesn’t have time for me to do that. 

I wish it were possible to jump to a particular day from a chart (tapping a dot). Otherwise I have to spend some time and look through my daily diary to anticipate questions my doctor might have since I don’t get any useful insights from the tiny dots and thin lines

Still just a week into it but this app truly does seem to cover all the bases. It’s awesome so far. 
Thanks!

reviews.t: So much better than I expected
reviews.b: I downloaded this app with the assumption that it was just a tracking tool. I thought it was great that I could send my data to an email address (like my doctor) and keep track of what I was eating and my symptoms. But I got to the sixth day of tracking and it showed me the food on my worst days, I’m completely hooked. My doctor has me on the low FODMAP/SCD SIBO specific diet and this app shows me which foods are part of the FODMAP list of foods I should avoid when I look at the foods on my worst days. I love that I didn’t have to look that up. Thank you so much for creating this app. Seriously so much.

reviews.t: wish it tracked period data- but otherwise good
reviews.b: I've been using it for 2 weeks now and have found it pretty easy to use. I'm interested in seeing how data is trended over time. Wish the app could also track menstrual cycle data though as that seems to be the biggest factor for me so now I use 2 separate apps to do the thing Cara is meant for!

reviews.t: Can’t even get into the App
reviews.b: Not because it’s broken. But because I can’t set it up for my daughter. She’s 6, and has special dietary needs. We don’t know what her triggers are and as she’s so little I can’t set up an account under her on this tool. 13 is the lowest age the app goes to. So, 3 stars as this would potentially be a perfect tool for us, but can’t use unless is set it up for me. My daughter can’t be the only one out there with special dietary needs.

reviews.t: Most comprehensive tracker I have found!
reviews.b:
I have been using Cara for only a few days so far but am impressed at how they were able to make it simple yet super comprehensive. I am able to track pretty much everything health related - which is very important to me with MS. I am really looking forward to getting more analysis from the app. You do have to commit to using it - garbage in, garbage out. But if you take the time to input everything, you will start to see correlations for sure. 

Keep up the great work!
This app has everything you can think of to track!
I’ve been wishing for an app exactly like this for long long time. It is easy to use, beautiful, and highly informative. Thank you.

Hi,
I love this app and all of the functionality of it, especially being able to add custom tags and all the different charting categories. There’s just one small bug that I’ve noticed. When someone charts “none” for bowel movements, it counts it as “1” in the weekly graph section. So when I chart that I’ve had none, the graph says I’ve had 1 when I look at it in the weekly format. Can that be fixed?
Great food diary app that incorporates data science. I’m excited to use it with my nutritionist.

I use this app everyday. It has helped me to see patterns with my eating and lifestyle habits. The only complaint I have about it is I wish you could enter time stamps in more than just intervals of 15 minutes. For example, if I eat at 11:50, I don’t want to document that I ate at 11:45. Otherwise, it’s a great app!

reviews.t: Has Potential to Be Best Food Tracker Available
reviews.b:
First, let me say that I love this app. I use it everyday and love the available features! I love that it suggests trigger foods AND that it can be set up to include food from the day before in my reactions. Beautiful interface, fairly intuitive layout. 

That said, I do have a couple suggestions (some of which I can use the notes section as a work around):

A couple suggestions:
—since this is tacking some pretty personal details, I wouldn’t mind having a password (or fingerprint scan) before opening the app. 
—would love to see a premade food library available so I don’t have enter every ingredient every time (app does have a way to save favorite meals, but I wish there was a library of meals Cara has already entered)
—would love to be able to track my weight too
—wish there was a way to indicate long term (like in a calendar) when I’m on a special diet (FODMAP, gluten free, vegetarian, etc)
—trigger food detection needs to be more specific. For example, xantham gum is on my bad list but its an ingredient in three meals I’ve recently eaten. I’d like to see which meals I had a reaction to—or if it was all three.

Health tracking always stresses me out but this app makes it so easy. The only thing would make it better would be more reminder notifications categories besides just meals ( water, medications). Was a bit time consuming to manually enter an alarm for all my waking hours to drink water.  I had a dedicated app for that before but I liked having my info all in one place so I decided to put up with the hassle
This is a great app and can help you track: stomach symptoms, bowel movements, food, mood, pain levels, food intake. Helps correlate issue together. Really great app!

reviews.t: Thank you this app is great
reviews.b: It helps a lot with keeping up with my health issue I want to keep an eye on. I’m really loving this app. My ability track the exact time of my med intake is a big help after I put in all the names/mg of my meds it is saved to a history list and all I do is tap the ones I’m taking at that moment (I don’t have to worry about overdosing myself anymore😅)

Only been using this app for a short time but my experience so far has been awesome.

- It's extremely easy to use. The user experience is really top notch. I'm stunned at how good it is.

- It's extremely versatile and feature-rich. They've really thought of just about everything in terms of ways to track your gastrointestinal health. Usually with apps of this type you quickly run into critical "wow I wish I could do x", but I haven't run into a significant situation like that so far. In fact there are so many features that I'm now tracking things I might not have even thought of.

- The graphic interface design is gorgeous. Usually you realize how important interface design is when you encounter a bad example of it, but in this case it's the opposite. Cara really made me appreciate the importance of great design by being beautiful. 

Can't recommend this app enough. Get it now!

reviews.t: Cara is on the right track!!!
reviews.b: I have been searching for an app like this for quite a while. Most of the ones I tried, ended up being deleted. I just started using it and liked it very much. I found out, the more you log in it, the easier it is to use and the more helpful it will work for you. The app still has improvements to be made. I would like to be able to use it on my iPad and see more integration with Apple-health......integration with MyFitnessPal would be a “😄home run”. All in all Cara is right on track!😃 I love this App!!!

This app seems messy at first glance, but it’s only because it allows you to log and store so much information! After a couple days of use, and with more data input, the app feels highly intuitive. I love that you can correlate any two sets of data. For a free app with no ads, it’s downright amazing.
I am looking forward to seeing how all of my behaviors are going to come together to show the correlations in how I feel.
I have severe food issues and this is great at tracking everything. It’s very easy to use. MUST GET if you have food issues - great at tracking your pain & symptoms.

I just found this today but feel very optimistic. I have a digestive motility disorder that affects my entertainment re digestive tract. I have had to keep a written journal because no other app has even come close to doing what I need it to. This has everything and it syncs with my phone health tracker. At this point I haven’t  used everything yet. So far nothing negative to note or anything I feel needs improvement.

This app is absolutely amazing! I am still attempting to figure out what is wrong with my stomach and the doctors have started to ask for food journals and symptom trackers. This app helps SO MUCH! 10/10 recommend to anyone that wants to track their gut and make their life so much easier

This app is pretty good, very helpful in tracking my daily habits. The only thing I don’t like is having to manually type in ingredients. It would be pretty nice if I could upload ingredients of my food by taking a picture or something. Take a picture and all the ingredients are uploaded. The ability to take more than one picture per meal. Otherwise I like it.

reviews.t: Helpful info and Easy to use
reviews.b: Cara makes it easy to track symptoms and correlate them to other life activities to get the big picture. The data export feature is easy to use and provides meaningful data. The custom tags feature lets you personalize the tracker.

I have Crohn’s disease, and I’ve been looking for an app that will allow me to track my diet, signs and symptoms, and my mood all in one app. This does an amazing job! It’s so customizable, it can be hooked up to the Apple health app on my phone, and it’s easy to use. It also gives me statistics regarding my health including the foods I eat on my best days and my worst days. This allows me to monitor what foods upset my stomach and which ones don’t in a very accessible and easy-to-understand way. It also allows me to correlate different aspects of my health and see if I notice any patterns that may clue me into things that I can be doing differently to help myself feel better. I was so overwhelmed with the thought of trying to figure everything out on my own, and this app does the overwhelming part for me. It allows me to simply focus on how I feel, and takes away some of the stress from everything else going on. I would recommend this app to any of my friends, family, and strangers; and best of all, it’s free. 10/10 would recommend!

reviews.t: Easy to use and cute interface
reviews.b: I like how you can document what you eat, current mood, bowel movements, exercise, sleep, and other health indicators all in one app! The app itself is very user-friendly and informational in terms of the metrics it spits out based on the user’s inputs.

reviews.t: So much better than counting calories!
reviews.b: This app is absolutely great! It has everything you could think of! Highly recommend.
This has helped me keep up with some of my stomach issues since my doctor wanted me to keep a journal, this is going to be the easiest way😊

Such a great app that allows me to keep track of symptoms and trigger foods for me. I’ve had a hard time finding the cause of my stomach pain and gastrointestinal symptoms but with this app it’s easier to communicate with my specialist.

I downloaded this app to use it as a food diary. My acupuncturist has asked me to log what I eat and how I feel. I have found it easy to navigate and I have been enjoying the added benefits as well. I find it to be a helpful tool to connect with my body.
This is a solid app. I’m looking forward to future iterations.
